expertFindings.section: W2.1 / W2.2 — identity manifest token shape
expertFindings.claim: The identity token block is specified as tier-2 roles only ("a base tree plus one overlay tree per rostered theme (mirroring `dtcg/semantic.<theme>.json`)"), but the landed identity contract is substantially tier-1 non-colour scales and tier-3 component/form tokens. An emitter built to this schema cannot reproduce the identities that already exist, so W2.2's acceptance line ("per-identity migration proofs — emitted output serves the demo suites green") is unachievable as written.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/semantic.light.json` roots are pinned in `packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts` (`SEMANTIC_ROOTS.light` = bg, border, color, control, ease, filter, focus, motion, scrim, shadow, state, surface, text, type). `space`, `radius`, `size`, `gap`, `inset`, `border.solid-*`, `weight` live in `dtcg/primitives.json`; `btn`, `flow`, `key`, `band`, `card`, `tag` live in `dtcg/component.json` — none of them reachable through a semantic overlay. The landed Freedonia identity overrides exactly those: `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/whitelabel/freedonia/brand-full.css` sets `--container-max: 960px`, `--flow-columns`, `--flow-gap: 30px`, `--key-align`, `--key-justify`, `--band-bg/--band-border/--band-pad`, `--density: 0.9`, `--gap-s/m/l`, `--inset-s/m/l`, `--control-pad-block/inline`, and the whole `--type-heading-1…7` ramp. `packages/design/oak-design-system/brand.css` §7/§7b/§7c publish these (density, `--radius-control`, `--size-target`, `--border-solid-m`, `--tag-radius`, `--card-radius`, `--btn-radius`) as the identity surface. The owner's standing requirement also names spacing explicitly ("design tokens for colour/typography/spacing and the other dimensions").
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the manifest token block as a full tier-spanning tree set — tier-1 non-colour scales, tier-2 roles, tier-3 component/form tokens — with the permitted root set enumerated per tier and the tier-referencing direction (component → semantic → primitive/palette) enforced by the schema. Name `brand.css`'s published surface as the derivation source for the required-field list, and make "every token brand.css publishes has a manifest home" a red-proven W2.1 fixture.

expertFindings.section: W2.1 / W2.4 — orthogonal contrast and colour-vision axes
expertFindings.claim: The stated token shape cannot express the axis composition the Director confirmed. Polarity is authored as light/dark arms, but the non-polarity overlays (high-contrast, colour-safe) are single-valued in the shape the plan mirrors — so composing them with polarity necessarily re-pins a light canvas. The plan states the goal ("a dark-preferring user who requests more contrast is never forced onto a white canvas") without the mechanism that produces it.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/colors_and_type.css:598-601` — `[data-theme='high-contrast'] { color-scheme: light; --bg-primary: var(--oak-white); … }`, flat single values, and the same at `:690-692` for colour-safe. The base roles are polarity pairs (`--bg-primary: light-dark(var(--oak-white), var(--oak-black))`, `:301`), so any flat HC/colour-safe override wins over both arms. `dtcg/semantic.high-contrast.json` (71 leaves) and `dtcg/semantic.colour-safe.json` (12 leaves) mirror that single-valued shape. W2.1 says only "polarity pairs authored as light/dark arms"; nothing requires the contrast and colour-vision overlays to be authored as arm pairs too.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State in W2.1 that EVERY axis overlay is authored in polarity-arm form (or that overlays are polarity-indexed), so a composed state resolves to `light-dark(hcLight, hcDark)`; add a rejection fixture for a contrast or colour-vision overlay that supplies only one arm, and make W2.4's acceptance assert the dark×more-contrast composition paints a dark canvas rather than only that it "resolves".

expertFindings.section: W2.5 — per-identity gate matrix, leg (i)
expertFindings.claim: The contrast leg composes "base ⊕ overlay" (singular) per identity × theme, but W2.1 explicitly makes dark × colour-safe and dark × more-contrast reachable states. Those composed states are therefore renderable and ungated, and the first one already fails AA on the landed values.
expertFindings.evidence: Verified composition: colour-safe sets `--text-success: var(--oak-ci-blue)` (#0072b2) and `--text-error: var(--oak-ci-vermilion-deep)` (#b34700) (`colors_and_type.css:693-694`, palette at `:137-140`); dark sets `--bg-primary` to `--oak-black` (#222222). Computed ratios: text.success 3.07:1, text.error 2.89:1 — both below the AA 4.5 text floor. Both pairs are already in the gated manifest (`dtcg/contrast-pairings.json`: `{text.success, bg.primary, text}` and `{text.error, bg.primary, text}`), and they pass today only because colour-safe composes over the light base (5.19:1 / 5.50:1). The landed gate composes one overlay per theme by construction: `packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-contrast.ts` iterates `OVERLAY_TREES` = {dark, high-contrast, colour-safe} against `semanticLight`.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make the contrast leg's cell set the full reachable axis product (identity × polarity × contrast × colour-vision), not identity × named theme; state the N-way merge order the emitter and the gate both use; and seed the acceptance with the dark×colour-safe case above as a red-then-green fixture so the gate is proven to bite on a composed state.

expertFindings.section: W2.4 — the `prefers-contrast` route
expertFindings.claim: The route is described as new behaviour landing here, but it already exists in the kit runtime; the plan adds a second, CSS-only implementation on a premise that is factually false, and no story amends the existing JS route — which, left as-is, re-forces the light canvas under the axis model and so defeats the Director's constraint.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:82-94` implements `auto()` returning the flat `'high-contrast'` name on `matchMedia('(prefers-contrast: more)').matches`; it is applied pre-paint at `apply(stored() || auto() || null)` and re-applied by a live `change` listener (`:120-129`). The plan's premise — "the runtime always writes the attribute when JS runs" — is false: `apply()` does `delete el.dataset.theme` when the value is null (`:66-69`), and the file header states "no choice = no attribute"; the plan's own W6.1/EX1 asserts the no-attribute default as a named invariant, contradicting W2.4. W2.4's negative cells ("explicit light / dark / colour-safe + `contrast: more` → high-contrast NOT applied") pin the current flat behaviour for an explicit-dark user, which is the exact outcome the composition goal forbids.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Replace the duplicate-route framing: name the amendment of `oak-theme.ts`'s `auto()` (contrast becomes an axis value written to its own attribute, never the flat theme name) as an explicit W2.4 acceptance line, correct the always-writes premise, and restate the negative cells as "an explicit POLARITY choice plus `contrast: more` composes to dark + more-contrast; an explicit CONTRAST choice suppresses the OS contrast signal" — with the JS-on and JS-off routes asserted to agree.

expertFindings.section: W0.2(b) — the dark-link-on-lemon token cure
expertFindings.claim: The two halves of the acceptance line are mutually exclusive. The named default cure is a band-scoped re-point, but the contrast manifest has no scope concept, so the pairing that "joins `dtcg/contrast-pairings.json`" would resolve the global `text.link` — reasserting the 4.48:1 failure and reddening the gate at the moment the acceptance requires it green.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/contrast-pairings.json` holds 42 pairs, every one of shape `{foreground, background, context}` with global token dot-paths (verified by key-shape census); `packages/design/design-tokens-core/src/contrast-types.ts` `ContrastPair` has no scope/selector field, and resolution is over the composed theme tree (`design-system-contrast.ts`). KNOWN-ISSUES item 13 records the pairing as 4.48:1 gate-measured with the cure explicitly scoped ("it must re-point `--text-link` in that band's scope").
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name a scoped role token (e.g. `text.link-on-decorative-5`, authored in both polarity arms and declared in the band scope) as the default cure, pair THAT token in the manifest, and re-baseline 42 → 43 against it — or state that the manifest gains a scope field as part of this story.

expertFindings.section: W0.1 gap census (EX10) / W4.4 type-coverage check
expertFindings.claim: The `$type`-completeness cure as stated is unimplementable against the landed trees: 85 leaves carry neither `$type` nor an alias `$value`, and DTCG 2025.10 defines no type that covers their values. A check "failing on any unresolvable leaf" would either red the build permanently or force deliberate mis-typing via group-level `$type`.
expertFindings.evidence: First-hand census of `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/`: untyped non-alias leaves — primitives 2, semantic.light 37, semantic.dark 3, semantic.high-contrast 6, component 37 (total 85). Examples: `state.hover = color-mix(in oklab, currentColor 8%, transparent)`, `filter.icon = invert(1)`, `flow.columns = 1fr`, `key.align = left`, `btn.pad = {control.pad-block} {control.pad-inline}`, `focus.ring = 0 0 0 {border.solid-l} {oak.color.black-true}, …`. The live DTCG 2025.10 format spec defines only color, dimension, fontFamily, fontWeight, duration, cubicBezier, number and the six composite types, defines no type for arbitrary CSS values or `color-mix()`, and states untyped tokens MUST be treated as invalid. The export's own contract already declares the deviation: `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/README.md` — "`$type` is heuristic … composite values (shadows, font shorthands) omit it".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split the census row: (a) leaves whose type is inferable by alias or group inheritance — gate at 100%; (b) leaves whose value has no DTCG type — carry an explicit recorded disposition (`$extensions` vendor annotation or a named exclusion list with a pinned count as the drift net), and scope W4.4's type-coverage check to class (a) with class (b) rendered as specimens.

expertFindings.section: W2.2 — the Oak CSS→DTCG projection generator
expertFindings.claim: The story mints a second CSS→DTCG generator for Oak. One already exists (studio-side) and its output is the input to the landed four-theme contrast gate. The plan states no authority relation, parity check, or sunset between the two generated Oak projections, so the estate ends with two derived Oak token trees gated independently — an SSOT fork inside a plan whose thesis is single-sourcing.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/README.md`: "Machine-readable … JSON, generated from the CSS source of truth (`colors_and_type.css`, `components.css`, `styles.css`). The CSS is canonical; regenerate these files after any token change — do not hand-edit." ADR-213 §2 states the same inversion. The landed gate consumes those trees: `packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-contrast.ts` imports `@oaknational/oak-design-system/dtcg/*.json`. W2.5 then gates "the identity's emitted token projection" — for Oak, the new W2.2 output — while the plan keeps Stage B convergence explicitly out of scope, so the export path stays live.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the relation explicitly: either the repo generator REPLACES the studio one for repo consumption (with the design-sync contract amended and the dual-gate window's input re-pointed in the same landing), or W2.2's acceptance carries a mechanical parity assertion between the two Oak projections with a named sunset condition. `replace-dont-bridge` should be applied by name.

expertFindings.section: W2.2 emitted namespace / W2.4 "identity-supplied palette slots"
expertFindings.claim: The namespace rule misstates the landed tiering and contradicts W2.4. It says bare names are tier-2/3 and `--oak-*` is reserved to tier-1 primitives — but tier-1 non-colour primitives are bare-named, so the rule mis-classifies them; and W2.4 simultaneously requires high-contrast and colour-safe to reference "identity-supplied palette slots", which are precisely the `--oak-*` tier the same paragraph forbids identities from emitting and which `brand.css` declares private.
expertFindings.evidence: Tier-1 non-colour primitives are bare: `colors_and_type.css:174` `--space-8: 8px;`, `:248` `--size-target: 48px;`, `:441` `--radius-control: var(--radius-s);`. Tier-1 colour is `--oak-*` (`:44-89`). `packages/design/oak-design-system/brand.css` header: "Tier-1 --oak-* primitives and unlisted tier-3 internals are PRIVATE: do not override them; they may change." The landed identities honour that — `grep -c -- '--oak-'` in `studio-source/whitelabel/freedonia/brand-full.css` returns 0 (creature: 5). Today's HC block resolves overwhelmingly to `--oak-*` (`colors_and_type.css:598-680`), which is exactly what W2.4 wants replaced — but with what surface is unstated.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate the namespace rule against the landed three-tier CSS vocabulary (tier-1 = `--oak-*` colour primitives plus the bare non-colour scales; tier-2 = bare role names; tier-3 = bare component tokens), then decide and record whether identities own a per-identity tier-1 palette (and if so, its namespace and its relation to `brand.css`'s private-primitive clause) before W2.4's HC re-authoring depends on it.

expertFindings.section: W2.1 — polarity composition into `light-dark()`
expertFindings.claim: "Polarity pairs authored as light/dark arms the emitter composes into `light-dark()`" is colour-only and does not cover the landed polarity set. Non-colour polarity overrides cannot ride `light-dark()`, so the emitter needs a second route the plan never names — and an identity supplying only arms would silently lose them.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/semantic.dark.json` carries exactly three non-colour leaves — `filter.icon = invert(1)`, `filter.icon-inverted = none`, `filter.icon-on-btn-primary = none` — all untyped. ADR-213 §2's 2026-07-19 amendment states this directly: dark is "the 60 `light-dark()` second arms plus the three non-colour `filter.*` overrides the §Dark block carries, `light-dark()` being colours-only". The landed CSS carries them in the `[data-theme='dark']` block and the `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) [data-theme='system']` block (`colors_and_type.css:580-592`).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State both emission routes in W2.1/W2.2: colour polarity pairs → `light-dark()`; non-colour polarity pairs → the attribute block plus its `prefers-color-scheme` twin for the system value. Add a fixture identity carrying a non-colour polarity override and assert both blocks are emitted.

expertFindings.section: W2.7 — off-horizontal token shape
expertFindings.claim: Composing tilt into `transform` at emission will clobber the kit's existing `transform` declarations (last-declaration-wins on a single longhand), and the story carries no acceptance line for the new `tilt` root against the two hand-pinned root allow-lists it must pass.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/components.css:504` `transform: translate(var(--space-2), var(--space-2));` plus seven glyph rotations at `:637, :685, :842, :847, :899, :903, :908` — the same seven instances the plan disposes of in the gap census. Root allow-lists that a new `tilt` root must enter: `SEMANTIC_ROOTS` in `packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts` (hand-pinned, per theme, enforced by `validateTreeRoots`) and ADR-213 §2's enumerated Stage-B export root set. §Relationships lists no ADR obligation for W2.7.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Specify emission onto the independent `rotate` property (CSS Transforms Level 2), which composes with an element's existing `transform` instead of replacing it, with a red-proven cell on an element that already carries a transform; and add the `SEMANTIC_ROOTS` re-baseline plus the ADR-213 §2 root-set amendment as W2.7 acceptance lines.

expertFindings.section: W2.3 — theme roster generation into the kit runtime
expertFindings.claim: "Emit-into-consumer codegen" has no available mechanism for the kit runtime: its source is deliberately import/export-free so `tsc` emits a classic script, so a generated roster module cannot be imported into it, and the emitted file is byte-parity-gated against a hand-authored source. The theme-№N falsifier depends on this mechanism.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:24-27`: "Script-kind source by design: no imports/exports, so tsc emits a classic browser script (an ESM emit would break the synchronous pre-paint contract)." The union and membership list are literals in that file (`:31`, `:48` `const THEMES: OakThemeName[] = [...]`). Parity is gated by `packages/design/oak-design-system/src/emitted-runtime-parity.integration.test.ts` against the committed root `oak-theme.js`.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the mechanism explicitly — either a marker-delimited splice into `src/oak-theme.ts` with the splice region asserted generated-only, or promote the whole file to a generated artefact with its authored logic moved to a template — and state how the byte-parity gate stays meaningful across the generated region.

expertFindings.section: W3.0 — ADR-213 §3 amendment (Director ruling 2 fidelity)
expertFindings.claim: The ruling requires the studio seeds to keep their tier-3 token-sufficiency-proof role, "fixtures-guarded". The plan re-homes the fixtures-parity duty to the tier and redefines it as a class-selection contract for tier components, so the seeds' guard never lands and their no-drift claim stays constructional — the exact condition ADR-213 §3 says fixtures-as-parity exists to convert.
expertFindings.evidence: Backlog workstream text (`.agent/plans-backlog-2026-07/architecture-and-infrastructure/current/design-system-integration.plan.md`, `ws-fixtures-parity`): "fixtures-as-parity inside oak-design-system against the four compiled components — converts the no-drift claim from constructional to checked … at the owned-tier landing this duty migrates to the tier package's own tests; until then it binds as written." The plan re-homes it straight to W3.0/W3.1 and restates it as "a class-selection contract per prop combination, no longer an independent-implementation drift check". No fixtures-parity exists anywhere in the repo today (grep across `packages/design`, `demos`, `.agent/plans` returns only this plan's own references); the seeds are `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/components/{OakButton,OakIcon,OakSubjectChip,OakTag}`.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split the duty in W3.0: keep an independent-implementation drift check against the four studio seeds inside the kit workspace (the role the ruling preserves), and land the class-selection contract as a separate, named tier obligation. State explicitly whether the §1 move-out fires for a seed that is adopted by rewrite.

expertFindings.section: W2.1 — colour-safe rejection fixture
expertFindings.claim: The fixture "colour-safe default absent (defaults on observably)" is ambiguous between "colour-safe is present in every roster by default" and "colour-safe is applied by default". A schema fixture will harden whichever reading the implementer takes; the second reading would change Oak's rendering estate-wide.
expertFindings.evidence: The strategic parent's kernel wording is "colour-safe a sensible default inclusion" — inclusion in the roster. Applying it by default would repaint every success/error surface: `colors_and_type.css:693-696` re-points `--text-success`/`--text-error`/`--bg-success`/`--bg-error` to the Okabe-Ito set, and the landed runtime treats colour-safe as a selectable theme only (`src/oak-theme.ts:48`).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate the fixture as "a manifest whose theme roster omits colour-safe is rejected", and separately state the applied-by-default question as out of scope (or route it to the owner) rather than encoding it in a schema fixture.

expertFindings.section: Frontmatter gate 3 / W0.2(b) / W2.4 — KNOWN-ISSUES item 14
expertFindings.claim: The item-14 subtree-alias ruling is framed as a single decision taken before any high-contrast or colour-safe subtree renders, but W2.4 changes the breadth of the question being ruled on: composing contrast and colour-vision with polarity multiplies the number of theme blocks in which every dialect alias must be re-declared. Ruling on the pre-axis breadth would under-specify the post-axis obligation.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/KNOWN-ISSUES.md` item 14: ":root-declared aliases freeze under SUBTREE high-contrast / colour-safe theming … What stays open here is only the alias-block breadth question — re-declare every dialect alias per theme block, or narrow the subtree contract". The landed HC block already carries per-theme alias re-declarations for this reason (`colors_and_type.css:656-670`, `--surface-decorative-6-soft` and `--surface-amber-soft` with the explanatory comment). W2.4 converts the two flat blocks into composable axis blocks.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State in W2.4 that the item-14 ruling is taken against the POST-axis block set, or make the emitter's alias re-declaration mechanical (every alias whose inputs an axis block overrides is re-emitted in that block) with a red-proven fixture, so the ruling is about contract breadth rather than manual upkeep.

expertFindings.section: W3.0 / W3.1 — The React component tier (ADR-213 §3 amendment)
expertFindings.claim: The Director's ruling (2) is implemented unfaithfully: W3.0 asserts the studio seeds are "fixtures-guarded" as a present property and "unchanged in purpose", but no fixtures-parity guard exists, the plan re-homes the only workstream that would build one, and it redefines that duty so nothing guards the seeds. Separately, ADR-213's adoption mechanism deletes the seed at adoption, contradicting "seeds remain".
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L620-631: "the studio seeds remain the tier-3 token-sufficiency proof (peer consumption, fixtures-guarded, unchanged in purpose)" and "Fixtures-as-parity is RESTATED at its re-homing (EX25): under kit-class painting it is a class-selection contract per prop combination, no longer an independent-implementation drift check"; §Relationships L943 re-homes `ws-fixtures-parity` → W3.0/W3.1. First-hand: `find packages/design/oak-design-system -name "*fixture*"` returns nothing — no fixtures-parity exists today; the backlog todo `ws-fixtures-parity` is `status: pending` (`.agent/plans-backlog-2026-07/.../design-system-integration.plan.md:51`), reading "fixtures-as-parity inside oak-design-system against the four compiled components". ADR-213 §3 amendment (L346-352): "each adopted component moves out of `studio-source/` and under the full quality gate in the same change" — so adopting OakButton removes the very seed the plan says remains. The four seeds are real and token-consuming: `studio-source/components/OakButton/OakButton.jsx` styles entirely from `var(--btn-*)` inline.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split the re-homing: keep a kit-workspace fixtures-parity story that builds the seeds' guard (seed markup ↔ components.css token parity) and state explicitly that the four seeds STAY in `studio-source/` (the §1 move-out is not triggered for them — the same carve-out W1.2 already makes for pages), so that the adopted tier component is a NEW artefact rather than a moved one. Then W3.0's re-homed fixtures duty covers only the tier's class-selection contract, and the ADR-213 §3 amendment records the seeds' non-move explicitly.

expertFindings.section: W3.1 — Curated adoption (tier prop API / polymorphism)
expertFindings.claim: The tier's polymorphism decision names a slot that its own default construction library does not have, and the element-union constraint blocks the composition the two React demos need. `asChild` is Radix vocabulary; Base UI — which the same story makes the default for interactive families — composes only via a `render` prop. Constraining the rendered element union to `button | a` makes it a type error to render a tier component as a Next `Link`, so the showcase's and styled demo's cross-page navigation (an owner acceptance object) falls back to full page loads.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L648-650: "polymorphism via a render/`asChild` slot with the rendered element union constrained to `button | a` (EX24 — no `next/link` in the tier)"; §Decision log L934 repeats it. Same story L641-644: "Base UI headless primitives are the §3 default". Base UI composition docs (base-ui.com/react/handbook/composition, fetched 2026-08-03): "Use the `render` prop to compose a Base UI part with your own React components" — no `asChild` anywhere. ADR-213 §3 decision table: "Radix | Existing code only; no new adoption". W4.7 (L776-779) makes end-to-end browsing with "navigation, cross-page rhythm" the showcase's closing acceptance, and W1.4 names a multi-page set (lesson pages, front pages, worksheets).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the slot `render` (element-or-function), matching Base UI, and drop `asChild`. Restate the constraint at the DOM level rather than the React-element level: the tier asserts the rendered DOM element is `button` or `a` (testable in the rendered gate), which permits a consumer to pass `<Link href>` — the tier still imports nothing from `next`. Add an acceptance cell in W5.3/W4.2 proving a tier component rendered through a consumer-supplied `Link` keeps client-side navigation.

expertFindings.section: W3.1 / EX26 — tier prop API (`className`, style, custom-property hooks)
expertFindings.claim: "No `style` prop" and "a declared set of custom-property hooks the component sets on its root" have no stated prop channel between them. The kit's own documented icon mechanism is an inline custom property, so the first icon-bearing family has no route from consumer intent to the element.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L636-648: "consume kit classes with variants as props; `useState` state-mirroring deleted in favour of CSS state semantics; no `style` prop" … "the sanctioned VARIATION route is a kit modifier class or a declared set of custom-property hooks the component sets on its root, EX26". Kit `components.css:214` documents the general route as `<span class="oak-icon--mask" style="--icon-src:url(assets/icons/tick.svg)" aria-hidden="true">`; `oak-icons.css` header repeats it with `style="--icon-src:var(--i-tick)"`. Class-scoped setters exist only for a named subset (`components.css:989-1001`). The seed `OakButton.jsx` resolves icon URLs at runtime from `script[src*="_ds_bundle.js"]` — a mechanism that cannot survive into a published package, and no story replaces it.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the channel: the tier declares a closed, typed set of custom-property hook props (e.g. `icon`/`tone` mapped internally onto `--icon-src` via the element's own `style`), and the prohibition is narrowed to "no consumer-supplied arbitrary `style` prop". Add to W3.0's mapping-rule contract how a tier component resolves kit asset URLs across consumers (base-path prop, mask-by-token-name, or class-only icons), since the seeds' resolution mechanism does not port.

expertFindings.section: W3.2 — Theme runtime completion
expertFindings.claim: W3.2 names `applied()` as "the React adapter's store shape" without stating what happens to the choice-model snapshot the landed tier documents as a cure. Executed as written it risks reverting MCP-388: a control bound to the applied theme cannot distinguish an explicit choice from the OS-triggered high-contrast default. The accessor is also a duplicate — the kit already exposes the applied theme as `get()`, and the plan never says whether `applied()` renames, supplements or replaces it on a framework-neutral runtime consumed by four demos plus the MCP app.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L663-667: "The React adapter's store shape is named: an `applied()` scalar snapshot with its server-snapshot semantics stated…". First-hand, `packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts` exposes exactly `set/get/choice/themes/motion`; `get()` returns `current || stored() || auto() || 'light'` — that IS the applied theme. `packages/design/oak-design-react/src/oak-theme-store.ts` docblock: "The theme snapshot is the CHOICE model, never the applied html attribute… a select pinned to a real value in that state would misreport the page AND make the first click on that value a dead control", and "An applied-theme surface (and its mirror) can land at first materialised need as its own accessor."
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State both snapshots and their bindings: `choice()` remains the control's bound value (or, if the toggle-button control binds applied state, say so and carry the dead-first-click cell that proves the regression is absent). Say whether `applied()` is a new name for `get()` or an addition, and carry the kit-contract change through the same consumer census W2.3 builds, since `get()` has consumers outside this plan.

expertFindings.section: W4.6 — Tailwind discipline in the showcase
expertFindings.claim: The stated lint cannot see the invariant it enforces. The recipe class that makes a utility a silent no-op is applied INSIDE a tier component, so a JSX class-string visitor classifies `<OakButton className="p-2">` as an element with no kit class and permits it — exactly where the showcase's whole point (tier + Tailwind together) puts the risk.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L760-775: "an element bearing a kit recipe class carries no painting-category utility … elements without a kit class carry composition utilities only (EX23)"; dispositions EX15: "the invariant is linted via the JSX class-string visitor". W3.1 L645-647 has the tier accept `className` "merged after kit classes". First-hand, `.oak-btn` (components.css:271-283) sets `padding: var(--btn-pad)` and `gap: var(--btn-gap)` unlayered, so a passed `p-2`/`gap-1` is silently dropped and the lint permits it.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Give the lint a resolvable source of truth: the tier exports a manifest of component → root recipe class that the visitor consumes, so `<OakButton className=…>` is classified as a recipe-classed element. Alternatively promote the "planted computed-value cell" from a single example to a rendered-DOM check over the demo's pages (every element carrying an `.oak-` recipe class is asserted to have no losing utility), which is method-independent of the JSX shape.

expertFindings.section: W4.6 / Cross-demo acceptance — Tailwind consumption path
expertFindings.claim: No story adds Tailwind to the showcase, and no story states the `@theme inline` mapping ADR-213 mandates as the Tailwind consumption model. Without a mapping, the composition utilities the plan explicitly permits resolve to Tailwind's DEFAULT spacing and type scale — not kit tokens — which contradicts "styling sourced solely from the design system" and undercuts the rubric's spatial-rhythm criterion.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L773: "The arbitrary-value check lands in the SAME PR that adds Tailwind" is the only mention of the addition; no W4 story owns it. ADR-213 §3: "**Tailwind consumption** is a mapping, not an adapter: a `@theme inline` block aliasing utilities onto the design system's semantic role variables" — the plan never names `@theme inline`. First-hand, the hub's `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/app/globals.css:25-107` `@theme inline` block maps colour, font, radius, shadow and motion roles but contains NO spacing mapping, so `p-4`/`gap-6` there already resolve to Tailwind defaults. W4.6 also requires motion/transform utilities to "resolve to mapped role names" — a mapping the plan never creates. The showcase today has no Tailwind at all (`demos/oak-design-showcase/package.json` has no tailwind dependency; `app/globals.css:1-13` records the 2026-07-29 plain-CSS ruling).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Mint an explicit W4 story for the showcase's Tailwind adoption whose acceptance includes the `@theme inline` mapping (colour, type, spacing, radius, shadow, motion roles) and a check that every utility family the lint permits resolves to a kit role — i.e. Tailwind's default spacing/colour scales are disabled or fully overridden. Name spacing explicitly, since the existing hub precedent omits it.

expertFindings.section: W1.5 / W4 — first-light probe vs the Tailwind rebuild
expertFindings.claim: The wow-first sequencing has an unnamed re-implementation step: W1.5's probe pages are authored in the showcase's current plain-CSS path, then W4 re-implements the same pages in React + Tailwind. The owner approves pixels produced by one styling vocabulary and the plan lands them again in another, with a lint that bans painting utilities and (per the finding above) an unmapped composition scale — so "pixels identical" is not preserved by construction.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L392-398 (W1.5): "One or two pages from W1.4's set authored IN the existing showcase workspace against kit classes (no W2 identity machinery, no W3 tier — the Decision log's kit-class painting makes these pixels identical to their post-W3 form)" — the claim is scoped to W3 only, never to the Tailwind conversion. First-hand, the existing showcase is plain CSS with authored page-expression hooks (`demos/oak-design-showcase/app/globals.css`: `body { margin: 0 }`, `.hero-inner h1`, `.util .oak-select`) that Tailwind utilities would replace. W4.2 lands "the React/Tailwind page that greens them".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Either author the W1.5 probe on the final consumption path (add Tailwind in W1 as part of the probe's landing, which also front-loads the mapping), or state in W1.5 that the probe's approval covers composition and grammar only and add a pixel-parity acceptance line to W4.2 (screenshot comparison of the probe page before/after the Tailwind conversion) so the approved rendering is provably preserved.

expertFindings.section: W5.3 — Consumption through the tier (styled-components override mechanism)
expertFindings.claim: The stated override mechanism is verifiably insufficient. `&&` yields specificity (0,2,0), which TIES with the kit's state selectors and LOSES to its nested ones — so a styled override lands at rest and is non-deterministic or dead on hover/focus/active, the states most likely to be overridden. The acceptance cell only measures dev vs production, never a state.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L804-812: "`styled(TierComponent)` overrides use styled-components' `&&` specificity bump … with an acceptance cell asserting a styled override actually computes in `next dev` AND `next build && next start`". First-hand in `packages/design/oak-design-system/components.css`: `.oak-btn:hover` (line 294) is (0,2,0) and sets `background`, `border-color`, `box-shadow`, `text-decoration`; `.oak-btn:disabled .oak-btn__icon` and `.oak-card-link:hover .oak-card` (line 500) are (0,3,0). styled-components emits a single generated class, so `&&` is (0,2,0).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the required specificity as a function of the kit's actual maximum recipe specificity (measured from components.css at W5 open — today (0,3,0), so `&&&`), or better, route overrides through the EX26 sanctioned mechanism (kit modifier class / declared custom-property hooks) and reserve raw specificity bumps for demo-local chrome the kit does not cover. Extend the acceptance cell to assert an override computes in the `:hover` and `:focus-visible` states, not only at rest.

expertFindings.section: W0.1 (feature census) / W3.0 (mapping completeness)
expertFindings.claim: The component-class census domain is one file, so the "full mapping-decision coverage" reading being carded to the owner is scoped to roughly three-quarters of the kit's class vocabulary. The typography classes — the most obvious React tier candidates — fall outside the census, the completeness check, and therefore the W4.5 coverage matrix.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L195-197: the feature census takes "component classes from `components.css`"; W3.0 L616-618 makes completeness "a check consuming the W0.1 census fails when any class lacks a recorded decision (one row per class, zero unmapped)". First-hand counts of distinct `.oak-` classes: components.css 107, colors_and_type.css 28 (30 real selector lines at colors_and_type.css:720-800 — `.oak-heading-1..7`, `.oak-heading-light-1..7`, `.oak-body-1..4`, `-bold` variants, `.oak-code-*`, `.oak-scope`, `.oak-interactive`), print.css 16, oak-icons.css 3, styles.css 4, brand.css 5. W0.1's parity leg is a "distinct `.oak-` class count", which would not reconcile with a components.css-only census.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the census domain for classes by the same path-plus-exclusions discipline W0.1 already uses for pages: all kit-published stylesheets (components.css, colors_and_type.css, oak-icons.css, print.css, styles.css), with print/deck classes taking an explicit `owner-accepted-exclusion` disposition rather than being invisible. State the expected class count in the parity line so a shrinking domain is visible, and re-word the owner card at W3.0 to say which vocabulary "full" ranges over.

expertFindings.section: W3.3 — Identity runtime binding
expertFindings.claim: W3.3 specifies two mutually exclusive delivery mechanisms in one paragraph, and no story dispositions the landed identity implementation it replaces — whose docblock records deliberate decisions (no persistence; React 19 `<link precedence>` rejected on documented semantics) that W3.3 reverses without naming them.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L671-684: the kit trunk carries "pre-paint application, load-then-swap, persistence" while the delivery mechanism is "identity stylesheets present in the initial HTML and selected by attribute" — if all sheets are already in the initial HTML there is nothing to load, so load-then-swap is dead; if load-then-swap survives, sheets are not all present. First-hand, `demos/oak-design-showcase/components/useIdentity.ts` implements load-then-swap over an owned `<link>` and states: "Identity deliberately does NOT persist across reloads: persistence would need a second pre-paint bootstrap to avoid a flash of Oak brand" and records why React 19's `<link precedence>` was rejected. No plan story names `useIdentity` for retirement.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Pick one mechanism and delete the other from W3.3 (attribute selection over pre-present sheets is the one that composes with pre-paint and persistence; load-then-swap exists only because sheets are fetched on demand). Add an explicit retire-and-replace acceptance line naming `demos/oak-design-showcase/components/useIdentity.ts`, and state the selector shape the emitter must produce so identity blocks and `[data-theme]` overlay blocks do not tie at (0,1,0) and resolve by source order.

expertFindings.section: W1.5 / W4 / Cross-demo acceptance — the showcase's theme and identity control
expertFindings.claim: No story owns re-authoring the showcase's control surface, yet three separate constraints bind it: the owner's taste calibration rejects native form-control switchboards, EX28's axis model implies a two-axis or composed-preset control, and W4.3 requires exactly three named identities. The landed showcase switchboard is built from native selects, and W1.5's early probe — an owner wow checkpoint — renders in that same workspace.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L88-91 records "REJECTED — bare specimen grids, native form-control switchboards, monochrome first paint". L0 assigns the toggle-button pattern to W1.2 (the plain demo) only: "a toggle-button group in each page's masthead … never a native select (taste calibration)". W2.4 L508-511 only "FLAGS" the axis implication to the checkpoint notes. First-hand, `demos/oak-design-showcase/components/Switchboard.tsx` renders three `LabelledSelect` components (native `<select>`), and its docblock carries a body of hydration and geometry work ("the theme and motion selects render as DISABLED 'Page default' placeholders in their full option geometry", geometry pinned by `tests/showcase.spec.ts`) that a toggle-button re-authoring must re-solve.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a showcase control story (W1.5 or W4) with the same specificity L0 gave W1.2: the control's form, its pre-hydration honest state, the ≤2-activation reachability of high-contrast and colour-safe, the three-identity requirement, and — once EX28's axes land — whether the control is two-axis or preset-based. Name the existing `Switchboard`/`LabelledSelect` modules and their geometry tests in the W4.2 generated inventory so their dispositions are recorded rather than lost.

expertFindings.section: W5.3 — Consumption through the tier (thinness proof)
expertFindings.claim: The instrument named for the no-fork claim cannot detect the thing it claims to bar. A forked copy of a tier component inside the styled demo has, by definition, no import edge — which is exactly what a dependency-cruiser rule inspects.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L810-812: "Acceptance (`repo-safe`: demo suites; zero forked component copies — depcruise; the override cells)".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split the two claims: a depcruise `required` rule proves the demo DOES depend on `oak-design-react` (positive consumption); the no-fork claim needs a different instrument — e.g. the W4.5-style coverage matrix requiring each kit-covered recipe used in the styled demo to resolve to a tier export, or a lint barring locally-declared components whose root class is a kit recipe class.

expertFindings.section: W3.2 — Theme runtime completion (notification mechanics)
expertFindings.claim: The two notification clauses contradict each other, and the motion axis is left out. "Listeners fire from `apply()`" plus "call `apply()`, THEN emit" double-notifies; and `apply()` is theme-only — the motion axis has its own application function and its own closure cache, so a cross-context motion write leaves the React motion snapshot stale even after the bridge lands.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L659-663: "**listeners fire from `apply()`** — the single application point" then "on a storage event for the kit's keys, RESET the module-local cache from the incoming value (null on removal), call `apply()`, THEN emit". First-hand, `src/oak-theme.ts` has a theme `apply()` with cache `current`, and a separate `createMotion()` closure with `mapply()` and cache `mcurrent` — `mcurrent` is closure-local, not module-local, and `mget()` returns it in preference to storage.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the contract per axis: both `apply()` and `mapply()` notify, the storage bridge dispatches on key (`oak-theme` → reset `current` + `apply()`; `oak-motion` → reset `mcurrent` + `mapply()`), and emission happens once, inside the application functions. Add the motion arm to the two-context acceptance cell alongside the theme arm.

expertFindings.section: W3.4 — Server/client boundary policy
expertFindings.claim: The W4 exit check is stated in a form no demo can satisfy. Every showcase page carries an interactive theme/identity control, so a client bundle necessarily exists; the checkable invariant is that page and layout modules are server components.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan L689-692: "plus the W4 exit check that showcase page/layout modules remain server components (a render-level no-client-bundle assertion)". ADR-213 §3 states the real invariant: "Composed widgets are leaf `'use client'` files; pages and layouts stay server components." First-hand, `demos/oak-design-showcase/app/layout.tsx` is a server component while `components/Switchboard.tsx` opens with `'use client'`.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate the exit check as ADR-213 words it — no `'use client'` directive in any `app/**/page.tsx` or `app/**/layout.tsx`, asserted over source and over the build's server/client module graph — and drop "no-client-bundle".

expertFindings.section: W0.3 (composition envelope) + W4.2 (declared-sequence focus-order check)
expertFindings.claim: The reordering envelope leans on CSS `reading-flow` as "progressive enhancement per variant" while the only gate that judges order is a Chromium-only Playwright cell. `reading-flow` is Chromium-only and explicitly not Baseline, so every CSS-reordered variant will fail SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and SC 1.3.2 (Meaningful Sequence) in Firefox and Safari — and the gate as designed can never see it, because in Chromium `reading-flow` repairs the order before the comparator observes it.
expertFindings.evidence: MDN/caniuse (fetched live 2026-08-03): `reading-flow` is "Limited availability", experimental, Chromium 137+ only; MDN states it affects "the order in which they are rendered to speech and navigated to". `docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md` §CI Requirements pins the harness to "Playwright's headless mode with Chromium (default)". Zero occurrences of `reading-flow` anywhere in the repo today (grep across `packages/design`, `demos`, `docs`) — this is new behaviour the plan introduces. W4.2's cell "only collects rects and asserts the verdict", i.e. it observes the post-`reading-flow` order.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make the BINDING declared-sequence cell run with `reading-flow` inert (a `reading-flow: normal` override or a non-Chromium project), so the DOM-order fallback is what passes the gate; `reading-flow` then genuinely rides as enhancement. State in the W0.3 envelope that a variant is admissible only if its declared sequence is satisfied by DOM order alone.

expertFindings.section: W2.4 (`prefers-contrast` route, gate cells)
expertFindings.claim: The negative gate cell is unsatisfiable as written for the plain demo, and contradicts the same story's own honesty note. "explicit light / dark / colour-safe + `contrast: more` → high-contrast NOT applied, JS enabled and disabled" cannot hold with JS disabled: the stored choice lives in `localStorage`, so with no JS the runtime never writes `data-theme`, `html:not([data-theme])` matches, and high-contrast IS applied.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/oak-theme.js:50-59,95` — the explicit choice is read only from `localStorage` by the script; `apply()` is the only writer of `el.dataset.theme`. W2.4 itself states "the JS-disabled limitation (a stored explicit choice cannot be honoured without JS) gets a dated honesty note". W1.2 makes the plain demo "Static HTML", so no server-side cookie resolution is available to substitute (that route is offered only to the Next demos in W3.3).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Scope the JS-disabled arm to the POSITIVE cell only (no stored choice + `contrast: more` → high-contrast applies without JS). Re-state the negative cells as JS-enabled, and record the JS-disabled explicit-choice loss as the named limitation the honesty note already carries, with the demos that can cure it (cookie-resolved Next demos) named.

expertFindings.section: W0.6 (Hub browser proof surface)
expertFindings.claim: W0.6's acceptance ("the new suites green in CI at the ci.yml `test:a11y` leg") is in direct tension with its own remediation clause ("violations the new suites find are triaged fix-only per ADR-147 ... with fix stories named as W0 work"). Under ADR-147 zero-tolerance and the no-`skipRules` rule there is no third state: either the fixes land inside W0.6 (making it an unbounded, unslicable story against the plan's own single-story-PR discipline) or the suite lands red in a CI leg that runs repo-wide.
expertFindings.evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:230` runs `turbo run test:e2e test:ui test:a11y test:widget`; root `package.json:48` fans `test:a11y` across workspaces. ADR-147 §Standard: "Tolerance: Zero — no `skipRules`, no accepted violations". `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/package.json` has no `test:ui`/`test:a11y` today, so adding them enrols the hub in that CI leg immediately. W0.6 is also absent from W1's enumerated W0 gate set ("W0.1 census, W0.2(a)/(b) stabilise, W0.3 charter, W0.7 instrument v0, W0.8 re-homes, W0.9 hub pre-read"), so the remediation has no sequencing relative to anything.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Slice W0.6 route-by-route: each PR lands one route's Playwright/axe cells together with the fixes that make them green, so no red gate ever exists. Give the remediation set an explicit sequencing position (before the W6.2 hub checkpoint at the latest) and state the discovery-bounded scope.

expertFindings.section: W2.5(iii) (per-identity gate matrix) + W0.3 (demos-tier a11y DoD)
expertFindings.claim: The plan relocates the rendered per-identity × per-theme accessibility run onto a TEST-ONLY specimen carrier that is explicitly excluded from shipped surfaces, and no story restores a per-identity × per-theme axe run over the shipped composed pages. Composed-surface contrast defects — the exact class the kit already carries — are invisible on a specimen carrier, and the DoD floor it falls back to only requires light+dark.
expertFindings.evidence: W2.5(iii): "the carrier is a TEST-ONLY fixture route, excluded from shipped navigation, wow checkpoints, and the W4.5 matrix's demonstrating surfaces". The existing showcase does run the real matrix on the real page: `demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts:137-153`, over `IDENTITIES = ['oak','freedonia','creature']` × `PALETTE_THEMES = ['light','dark','high-contrast','colour-safe']` (`tests/apply-state.ts:21-22`). The floor the DoD points at is weaker: ADR-147 §Standard says "Both light and dark themes must pass independently". KNOWN-ISSUES item 13 (dark body links on `surface.decorative-5`, 4.48:1) is precisely a composed-page pairing no specimen grid surfaces.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add to the charter DoD an explicit shipped-page axis statement: axe runs over each demo's composed pages across identity × the full palette-theme roster (not just light/dark), with the pinned cell count. Keep the specimen carrier as an ADDITIONAL state-coverage leg, never the substitute.

expertFindings.section: W0.8 (shared instruments re-homed) + W0.3 (demos-tier a11y DoD)
expertFindings.claim: The non-axe accessibility instruments are not hoisted and the criteria they cover are not in the DoD, so three of the four demos would ship with axe-only proof for criteria axe cannot detect. axe ships no focus-indicator-contrast rule and no reflow rule; both instruments exist today but only inside the showcase workspace.
expertFindings.evidence: W0.8's move list is (a) the authored-CSS literal walker, (b) `validate-kit-assets`/`kit-asset-parity`, (c) the shared demos test harness "origin gate, hermetic cross-origin interception, apply-state" — it does not include `demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/focus-ring-contrast.ts` (+ its `.unit.test.ts`), which is where the SC 1.4.11 ring verdict lives (`tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts:12,45-97`), nor the 320px reflow measure (inline at `tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts:168-196`, comment: "SC 1.4.10 Reflow — axe ships no rule for it"). The W0.3 DoD additions list SC 2.4.11, 2.4.3/1.3.2, 1.4.13, 2.5.7, colour-alone and the 44px floor — no 1.4.11 focus-indicator contrast, no 1.4.10 reflow, no 1.4.12 text spacing. The cross-demo acceptance says only "visible focus", not focus contrast.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add the focus-ring contrast comparator and the 320px reflow measure to W0.8's hoist list so all four demos consume them, and name SC 1.4.11 (focus indicator), SC 1.4.10 (reflow) and SC 1.4.12 (text spacing — the type slots bake line-height into font shorthands) as DoD cells with their instruments.

expertFindings.section: W2.1 (forced-colours obligation), W2.5 (forced-colours cell), W2.10 (forced-colours render check)
expertFindings.claim: The plan multiplies forced-colours cells per identity × theme without adopting the estate's mandated forced-colours criterion-scoping pattern, and without truing the existing showcase cell that already diverges from it. Executed as written the new cells either report spurious contrast violations under an open upstream axe bug, or add an unscoped rule disable that the governance doc forbids.
expertFindings.evidence: `docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md` §"Contrast rules under forced colours" mandates: `disableRules(['color-contrast'])` on that mode ONLY, gated by `matchMedia('(forced-colors: active)')` (never a project name, so a dead emulation fails safe), paired with a self-retiring assertion tied to axe-core#3978 — and states "Any forced-colours project added elsewhere in the estate meets the identical facts and uses this same pattern". The showcase's existing forced-colors cell (`tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts:34-42`) calls the shared `expectNoAxeViolations`, whose only configuration is `.withTags([...])` (`tests/apply-state.ts:29`) — no scoping, no matchMedia gate, no self-retiring assertion.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the accessibility-practice forced-colours pattern as an explicit acceptance line on W2.5's and W2.10's forced-colours cells, and add truing the existing showcase helper to the W0.8 harness hoist (it becomes the shared helper) so the estate has one convention, not two.

expertFindings.section: W1.2 (theme control), W2.4 (theme-control surface implication), cross-demo acceptance
expertFindings.claim: The theme/identity control's accessible pattern is unspecified anywhere in the plan. "A toggle-button group ... real `<button>` elements" fixes the element but not the semantics: no group role decision (radiogroup vs toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`), no accessible name for the group, no selected-state exposure (SC 4.1.2), no keyboard model (roving tabindex vs all-tabbable), and no application of the plan's own "state is never colour alone" criterion to the control itself. W2.4 then routes the axis model's control implication ONLY to the wow-checkpoint notes — a visual judgement — so no accessibility criterion binds the one control that is the sole route to high-contrast and colour-safe.
expertFindings.evidence: W1.2: "a toggle-button group in each page's masthead ... real `<button>` elements wired to `oak-theme.js` `set()` by a small demo-local script, visible from page load (≤2 activations), keyboard-operable by construction". W2.4: "The THEME-CONTROL SURFACE implication of the axis model (a two-axis control, or composed presets) is FLAGGED in the wow-checkpoint notes ... no separate pre-emptive gate". Today's control is native selects (`#oak-identity-select`, `#oak-theme-select`, `#oak-motion-select`, `tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts:105,115`), which carry these semantics for free — the taste calibration rejects them, so the semantics must be re-supplied by hand. A set of buttons where exactly one is on is a radiogroup, not N independent `aria-pressed` toggles.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a charter DoD clause specifying the control's pattern against the ARIA APG: group semantics and accessible name, single-select state exposure, the keyboard model, and a rendered cell asserting name/role/value plus a non-colour selected indicator — applied identically wherever a theme or identity control renders in any of the four demos.

expertFindings.section: Cross-demo acceptance + W2.4 (JS-disabled note)
expertFindings.claim: colour-safe has no OS media signal, so with JS unavailable it is unreachable in every demo — and the plan never states this. The recorded honesty note covers only the loss of a STORED choice; it does not surface that the one theme built for a disability with no OS query is JS-only by construction, in the demo whose whole point is plain HTML+CSS.
expertFindings.evidence: `oak-theme.js:60-72` — `auto()` consults `prefers-contrast: more` only; there is no colour-vision media query in CSS. W2.4's CSS route is `@media (prefers-contrast: more) { html:not([data-theme]) { … } }`, i.e. high-contrast only. W1.2 wires the plain demo's control "by a small demo-local script". The cross-demo acceptance asserts "high-contrast and colour-safe reachable from the visible theme control" without qualifying the JS precondition.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Have the charter record a per-demo × per-axis reachability matrix with JS on and off (polarity: CSS; contrast: CSS + JS; colour-vision: JS only; motion: CSS + JS), and either name a no-JS route for colour-safe in the plain demo (e.g. an `:has()`/`:target`-driven selector or a URL-addressable variant) or carry the owner's recorded acceptance of the limitation.

expertFindings.section: W2.7 (off-horizontal) vs W2.5 (gate matrix)
expertFindings.claim: W2.7 asserts "the tilted identity's 320px reflow cell re-runs in W2.5", but W2.5 establishes no reflow leg at all — its four mechanisms are token-pair contrast, the CVD colour-safety leg, rendered a11y over the specimen carrier, and the pinned cell count. Reflow also cannot be meaningfully proven on a test-only specimen carrier. Rotation is a known SC 1.4.10 hazard (a tilted block's bounding box exceeds its untransformed width), so the identity the owner wants MOST off-horizontal is the one with no reflow proof.
expertFindings.evidence: W2.5 enumerates (i)–(iv) with no reflow mechanism. The only reflow instrument in the estate is inline in the showcase spec (`tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts:168-196`), asserting `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` and `minLeft === 0` per identity at a 320×900 viewport, and it runs against the real page, not a specimen route. The kit's own contract (`packages/design/oak-design-system/CLAUDE.md`) binds "Reflow: usable at 400% zoom / 320px width without loss".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add an explicit reflow leg to W2.5 (per identity × theme, over the shipped composed pages, not the specimen carrier) and re-point W2.7's sentence at it; include a tilt-specific cell asserting no transformed element pushes content left of the origin or past `clientWidth`.

expertFindings.section: W4.2 (generated instrument inventory, must-retain seed rows)
expertFindings.claim: The must-retain seed set names only three cells, leaving every other existing accessibility cell droppable "with reason" at the seat's discretion. The cells omitted are precisely the ones whose criteria axe cannot re-derive, so a compliant execution of W4.2 can silently retire real WCAG coverage.
expertFindings.evidence: W4.2 seeds "the `prefers-contrast` auto-select cell, the identity × system-under-dark-OS cells, and the inverted-band focus-ring cell". `demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts` also carries: the identity × theme AA matrix (lines 137-153, 12 cells), the per-identity 320px reflow cells (168-196), the forced-colors renderability cell (34-42), and the switchboard focus-ring cell in light and dark (100-118) — none of them named. The plan's disposition vocabulary is "retained verbatim / re-expressed / dropped with reason".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate the must-retain rule as a criterion rather than a hand list: any cell whose success criterion axe cannot detect (1.4.10 reflow, 1.4.11 focus-indicator contrast, forced-colours renderability, 2.4.3/1.3.2 order) is must-retain-or-re-express, never droppable; the three named cells become examples.

expertFindings.section: W2.5(ii) (colour-safety leg) + W2.1 (rejection fixtures)
expertFindings.claim: The CVD colour-safety leg has no declared theme axis while the mechanisms either side of it pin theirs explicitly, and the rejection fixture "colour-safe default absent (defaults on observably)" is ambiguous between "present in the roster by default" and "applied by default". SC 1.4.1 applies in every theme, so a leg that runs only against the colour-safe theme proves nothing about the themes users actually land on.
expertFindings.evidence: W2.5(i) says "per identity × theme"; (iv) says "the product over ALL declared axes — identity × theme × the OS-signal emulation set"; (ii) says only "over the identity's success/error/warning/selected role set". The landed default is light-first (`packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts:15`, `DESIGN_SYSTEM_THEMES = ['light','dark','high-contrast','colour-safe']`, "light first (the declared base)"), and `oak-theme.js:74` returns `'light'` as the final fallback — so "defaults on" is false of the landed system as read.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the CVD leg's axis as identity × theme (all rostered themes, not just colour-safe), and rewrite the rejection fixture to say which reading binds: colour-safe MUST be present in every identity's roster (rejection = absent from roster), with the default applied theme staying light.

expertFindings.section: W0.6 (Hub browser proof surface)
expertFindings.claim: W0.6 mischaracterises the hub's current accessibility surface as absent, and therefore never routes the standing `color-contrast` rule disable it contains. The hub already has a jsdom axe backstop that switches off the single rule most relevant to a demo carrying 548 untokenised colour values; the new browser suite is exactly the instrument that could measure it, but nothing in the plan requires the disable to be retired when it lands.
expertFindings.evidence: `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/components/a11y-axe.test.tsx:20` — `const axeOptions = { rules: { 'color-contrast': { enabled: false } } };` with the comment "colour-contrast needs a canvas jsdom does not provide; every palette pair on these surfaces is contrast-verified by reviewer recompute (§E ledger)". W0.6 states only "no `test:ui`/`test:a11y` scripts exist" (true — verified in `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/package.json`), omitting this. `docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md` §Rule Configuration: "No `disableRules` in any mode a rule's criterion applies to ... the ONLY sanctioned `disableRules` call is the forced-colours criterion scoping".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the existing jsdom backstop in W0.6, and make retirement of its `color-contrast` disable an acceptance line of the browser-suite landing (browser axe measures contrast, so the compensating manual recompute is no longer needed).

expertFindings.section: Frontmatter owner gate 3 (KNOWN-ISSUES item 14) + W0.2(b)
expertFindings.claim: An accessibility-required rendering is blocked behind an owner decision with a hard expiry and no stated default. If the gate expires unanswered on 2026-08-21, no surface may render a high-contrast or colour-safe subtree — which the token-reference page (W4.4, per-identity × theme swatches) and any side-by-side theme comparison will need.
expertFindings.evidence: Frontmatter gate 3: "the KNOWN-ISSUES item-14 subtree-alias ruling lands before any surface renders a high-contrast or colour-safe subtree ... expires: 2026-08-21". `packages/design/oak-design-system/KNOWN-ISSUES.md` item 14 already states an interim safe rule of its own: "until ruled, avoid dialect aliases inside HC/colour-safe _subtrees_ (use the `--surface-decorative-N` roles directly; they re-declare correctly)" — and names `--border-accent` and `--bg-selected` among the frozen aliases, both of which the CVD leg's "selected" role set would read.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Adopt item 14's own interim rule as the plan's stated default so the gate's expiry cannot block an accessibility-required render: subtree HC/colour-safe surfaces use `--surface-decorative-N` roles directly, with the alias-breadth ruling upgrading the surface later rather than gating it.

expertFindings.section: W2.4 — Theme overlays and axes re-architecture (gate cells)
expertFindings.claim: The W2.4 negative gate cell is unsatisfiable by the mechanism W2.4 itself names: with JS disabled, an explicit stored theme choice cannot suppress the CSS `prefers-contrast` route, so "high-contrast NOT applied … JS disabled" can never go green. A seat executing this writes a test that cannot pass, or silently drops the JS-disabled arm.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan text (W2.4): scoping mechanism is `@media (prefers-contrast: more) { html:not([data-theme]) { … } }` and "the runtime always writes the attribute when JS runs"; the same paragraph concedes "the JS-disabled limitation (a stored explicit choice cannot be honoured without JS)". Two sentences later: "Gate cells: … the negative cells (explicit light / dark / colour-safe + `contrast: more` → high-contrast NOT applied, JS enabled and disabled…)". With JS off there is no `data-theme`, so `html:not([data-theme])` matches and high-contrast IS applied. Verified first-hand that `prefers-contrast` today is JS-only — `<repo>/packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:87` (`matchMedia('(prefers-contrast: more)')` inside `auto()`); zero `prefers-contrast` occurrences in the kit's CSS. The plain demo (W1.2) has no server-side attribute route at all, so no cookie/SSR escape exists there.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split the cell set explicitly: the negative cells run JS-ENABLED only (explicit choice → attribute → media rule loses); the JS-DISABLED arm becomes a POSITIVE cell asserting the documented degraded behaviour (no stored choice honoured; `contrast: more` yields high-contrast) so the honesty note has a describing test rather than a contradicting one. Per `testing-strategy.md` §Rules "No conditional tests", the two behaviours are two deterministic cells, never one cell with an environment-dependent expectation.

expertFindings.section: W2.3 — Theme roster generation (theme-№N falsifier) / W2.6
expertFindings.claim: The theme-№N falsifier is not constructible in the form its acceptance line demands. "The falsifier red-then-green as a standing CI case" plus EX5's "zero edits outside the pinned expectations module, plus the required reviewed re-baseline inside it" leaves only two implementations, both defective: (a) permanently mint the fake theme, which then ships into the generated roster, the kit runtime union, the demo label maps and the visible theme control the owner browses at every wow checkpoint; or (b) have the test edit `design-system-expectations.ts` at run time, which is filesystem mutation inside a test. The identity falsifier received exactly the containment this one lacks.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W2.3: "The theme-№N falsifier (W2.6): a config-minted test theme reaches `data-theme`, the matrix, and the labels with zero edits outside the pinned expectations module, plus the required reviewed re-baseline inside it (EX5). Acceptance (`repo-safe`: the falsifier red-then-green as a standing CI case…)". `dispositions.v2.1.md` EX5 confirms the pinned module stays hand-pinned. First-hand: `<repo>/packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts:15,24,35,67,89` pins `DESIGN_SYSTEM_THEMES`, `THEME_GATE_LEVELS`, per-theme `SEMANTIC_ROOTS`, `EXPECTED_MANIFEST_PAIR_COUNT = 42`, `EXPECTED_COMPARAND_SIZE = 167` — a minted theme moves several of these. Contrast W2.6(a)/EX41, where the identity falsifier is explicitly "rendered on a TEST-ONLY fixture route … excluded from shipped builds and the W4.5 demonstrating-surface set". No equivalent isolation is stated for the theme case. A run-time edit of a committed source module also trips `test-immediate-fails.md` items 4 and 22.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Give the theme falsifier the same containment shape as the identity one: the roster generator takes its theme list as an INJECTED parameter (ADR-078 DI), the standing case mints theme №N into a fixture roster and asserts propagation to `data-theme`, the gate-matrix cell derivation and the label map through the generator's outputs — with the pinned expectations module supplied as a fixture literal, never the repo file. State the "zero edits outside the pinned module" property as the CONSTRUCTION the test exercises (a fixture roster), not as a process claim. Cite `testing-patterns.md` §"Untestable-Without-Prohibited-Mechanisms Is a Product-Code DI Defect": if the falsifier cannot be written without mutating a committed module, the injectable seam is the missing product code.

expertFindings.section: W4.5 — Feature-coverage matrix, generated
expertFindings.claim: The coverage matrix — the plan's exit checklist — has no stated test↔row binding mechanism, and one of its four failure modes is unscoped in a way that makes it permanently red. "An executed test bound to no row" fails for every plumbing test in the run (validator unit tests, tier store tests, comparator tests), none of which demonstrate a census feature. And rows dispositioned `owner-accepted-exclusion` by W0.1 have no demonstrating surface by construction, yet mode one fails on exactly that.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W4.5: "fails on: a census row with no demonstrating surface; an id resolving to zero executed tests (orphan); an id resolving to a non-passing test; an executed test bound to no row — with a zero-tests-scanned non-vacuity leg." The word "id" is never defined anywhere in the plan — no title tag, annotation, or manifest convention is named. W0.1 defines four dispositions including `owner-accepted-exclusion`; W4.3 only obliges `express-composed` and `fold-into-composition` rows to land on a surface. First-hand, the estate's only precedent for tagging tests is the Playwright title-tag idiom (`@a11y` in `<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts`, split by `--grep` in that workspace's `package.json`), which the plan does not adopt or reject.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the binding convention in W4.5's own text (a census-row id token in the test title, matching the estate's `@a11y` tag precedent, or a committed per-page manifest keyed by row id), and scope the fourth failure mode to the TAGGED population ("a test carrying a row token that resolves to no row"), never to every executed test. State the disposition-to-obligation map so `owner-accepted-exclusion` and `reference-tier` rows resolve without a per-page surface. Keep the zero-tests-scanned non-vacuity leg — it is the right guard and matches the landed `validate-authored-css.ts` precedent ("scanned zero authored .css files — the walk is broken, not the CSS clean").

expertFindings.section: W4.5 (EX45 report consumption) and §Cross-demo acceptance
expertFindings.claim: The matrix gate's stated input — "the runners' JSON reports from the same `pnpm check` run" — cannot be relied on: every relevant turbo task is cached with `outputs: []`, so on a cache hit no report is written or restored. The gate then either fires its own zero-tests-scanned leg (spurious red on any warm `pnpm check`) or reads a stale report from an earlier run and passes vacuously against out-of-date results.
expertFindings.evidence: First-hand, `<repo>/turbo.json`: `test` (line 363) `"outputs": []`, `"cache": true`; `test:ui` (line 448) `"outputs": []`, `"cache": true`; `test:a11y` (line 454) `"outputs": []`, `"cache": true`. Root `check` runs `turbo run --continue … test test:ui test:a11y …` and only afterwards `pnpm repo-validators:check`. The showcase's Playwright reporter today is `reporter: [['list']]` (`<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/playwright.config.ts`) — no JSON report is produced at all.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make the report an explicit acceptance line of W4.5: add the JSON reporter to each demo's Playwright config and the vitest JSON reporter to the relevant workspaces, declare the report paths in the corresponding `turbo.json` `outputs` arrays so a cache hit RESTORES them, and have the gate assert report freshness (a run/commit stamp it compares against `git rev-parse HEAD`) in addition to the non-vacuity leg. Without the freshness assertion the gate is a decorative assertion in the sense of `testing-strategy.md` §"Prove the guard bites".

expertFindings.section: W0.1 — Page + feature census, generated and dispositioned
expertFindings.claim: The census's bidirectional describing test has no conformant home under the mechanism split the same story names. A "planted class/page/token-root in a fixture tree" exercises the WALKER's traversal, but the walker is a script (excluded from vitest discovery by the estate's own script rule), and a vitest file that walks a fixture tree is a validator wearing a test harness. As written, the story's headline guard is either unwritable or written in a prohibited shape.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W0.1: "Mechanism split (EX44): a pure classifier (rows in → dispositioned census out) with unit tests, plus a workspace-owned walker script wired into `pnpm check`. Describing tests are BIDIRECTIONAL (EX43): a planted class/page/token-root in a fixture tree MUST appear in the generated census (red = it does not)". The cited precedent is exactly the classifier/script split: `<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/css-literal-values.ts` (pure, unit-tested) plus `tools/validate-authored-css.ts`, whose `authoredCssFiles()` recursion is UNTESTED and guarded only by an in-script non-vacuity check. `<repo>/vitest.config.base.ts` states scripts are "intentionally OUTSIDE this include surface — see ADR-168 §5 … A `*.test.ts` under `scripts/` does not run by design".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Move the traversal boundary: the classifier takes an injected FILE LIST (paths + contents) per ADR-078, so the planted case becomes a literal-input unit test (`testing-tdd-recipes.md` §"Validator Script vs Integration Test" — pure helper unit-tested plus a standalone runtime script). Keep the walker to `readdirSync` + hand-off, guarded by the non-vacuity leg the landed precedent already uses, and state the method-independent parity counts as walker-level acceptance lines rather than as tests.

expertFindings.section: W4.4 — The token-reference page (parity test)
expertFindings.claim: W4.4's parity test is tautological as scoped: the page content is generated from the emitted token projection, and the plan never names what the generated content is compared AGAINST — while explicitly ruling out the one method-independent comparand available (runtime computed values). Reproducing the projection from the projection validates internal consistency only.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W4.4: "Content generated at BUILD time from W2's per-identity emitted token projections … and never runtime `getComputedStyle` as the value source. The parity test is SCOPED (EX9): per identity × theme over the statically-resolvable class (the landed `toHexComparand` filter)". No second side of the comparison is named. `testing-strategy.md` §Acceptance Value-Proxies and `testing-patterns.md` §"Acceptance Value-Proxies" both require an independent ground-truth measure and instruct rejecting the framing at plan-author time. The landed filter exists (`<repo>/packages/design/design-tokens-core/src/contrast-resolve.ts:140`), which fixes the SCOPE but not the comparand.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the two sides in W4.4: the generated page content on one side, and the RENDERED computed value read in the browser (per identity × theme) on the other — `getComputedStyle` is barred as the content SOURCE but is precisely the independent measure the parity claim needs. Pin the cell count as already planned, and keep the recorded dispositions for `runtime-computed`/composed-shorthand tokens as explicit no-assertion rows.

expertFindings.section: W1.5 / W3 / W4 — approved pixels beneath later landings
expertFindings.claim: The plan's central value — owner-approved pixels — has no mechanical regression guard anywhere. W1.5 asserts the probe pages' pixels are "identical to their post-W3 form" and W3 families "later land beneath already-approved pixels", but nothing tests that. The only detector of a regression on an approved page is another owner sitting, which the plan explicitly batches and rations.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W1.5: "the Decision log's kit-class painting makes these pixels identical to their post-W3 form" — no acceptance line binds it. W3 preamble/W4.2 land migrations "beneath already-approved pixels". First-hand: zero `toHaveScreenshot` / screenshot-baseline usage in the estate's demo suites (`<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase.spec.ts`, `showcase-a11y.spec.ts`; `screenshot: 'only-on-failure'` in `playwright.config.ts` is diagnostics, not a baseline). `testing-strategy.md` §Browser Proof Surfaces names "Visual regression — screenshot comparison baselines" as one of the four required browser proof categories for UI-shipping workspaces; the plan carries the other three and silently omits this one.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make the checkpoint's output executable: at each wow checkpoint that records a PASS, land a screenshot baseline for that page in the same PR (identity × theme cells sampled per the page-set artefact), so every subsequent W3/W4/W5 landing beneath it is gated by pixel diff. This is the atomic-landing invariant applied to an owner-held criterion — the approval and the test that preserves it travel together — and it turns the fidelity register's PASS rows into something a later commit can falsify.

expertFindings.section: W2.5 — Per-identity gate matrix (pinned cell count)
expertFindings.claim: The pinned cell count is unresolvable as specified and internally inconsistent. Clause (iv) pins "the product over ALL declared axes — identity × theme × the OS-signal emulation set" but the OS-signal emulation set is never enumerated anywhere in the plan, so no reviewer or CI can compute the expected number; and clause (iii) scopes the rendered a11y runs to "per identity × theme", a different population. Executed literally over a state-matrix specimen carrier the product runs to hundreds of axe passes.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W2.5(iii)/(iv). For scale, first-hand: the CURRENT single-page suite is 3 identities × 4 palette themes = 12 axe cells plus 3 system cells plus 3 reflow cells (`<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts`, `identity × theme matrix` / `identity × system theme (dark OS)` / `reflow at 320px` blocks). W2.1 declares OS bindings for `prefers-color-scheme` and `prefers-contrast`, W2.1 adds a forced-colours obligation and W6.1 adds motion — 3 × 4 × (2×2×2×2) is 192 cells on the specimen carrier alone, before the composed page suites in four demos.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Enumerate the OS-signal emulation set by name in W2.5 and split the pin per leg: full product for the polarity × contrast pair (the composition the axis model exists to prove), named single cells for forced-colours and reduced-motion, and a separate pinned count for the specimen-carrier leg versus the composed-page leg. A pinned count that cannot be computed from the plan is not a non-vacuity guard; enumerating the axes as literal arrays also keeps the suite inside `no-conditional-tests.md` §"NOT conditional (allowed)" deterministic enumeration.

expertFindings.section: W1.2 / §Cross-demo acceptance — "zero raw literals" for the plain demo
expertFindings.claim: W1.2's claim that "W0.8's walker covers the workspace by construction" is false for a plain HTML demo: the landed walker inspects `.css` files only, and the sibling half of the instrument is a JSX-only ESLint rule. Inline `style="…"` attributes and `<style>` blocks in the plain demo's `.html` files are ungated, so the first demo the owner sees can violate the plan's own zero-literals criterion with every instrument green.
