expertFindings.evidence: First-hand: `<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/validate-authored-css.ts` — `authoredCssFiles()` collects only `entry.name.endsWith('.css')`. `<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/eslint.config.ts:60,65` bans the style attribute via `JSXAttribute[name.name='style']` and `JSXElement[openingElement.name.name='style']` — JSX selectors that cannot match `.html`. The config's own message names the two halves: "bypasses both halves of the no-hardcoded-values instrument (the .css walk and the style-attribute ban)". Plan W1.2 states the pages are "Static HTML + kit stylesheets + `oak-theme.js`" and "Zero raw literals (W0.8's walker covers the workspace by construction)".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add the HTML arm to W0.8's re-homing story as an explicit acceptance line: the literal walker also parses `.html` `<style>` blocks and `style=` attributes through the same pure `findLiteralDesignValues` classifier, red-proven on a planted hex in a fixture page (the planted-hex red proof EX37 already requires for identity layers). Correct W1.2's "by construction" sentence to name the HTML arm.

expertFindings.section: W6.1 — Cross-demo verification (first-frame capture cell)
expertFindings.claim: The first-frame cell names an observable with no mechanism. "A FIRST-FRAME capture cell (EX36) asserts no frame paints the base palette on identity or theme deep-links" — Playwright exposes no frame-accurate hook, so the natural implementations are timing-based (a screenshot raced against paint), which is the nondeterminism class the estate's wall-clock ruling deletes rather than tunes.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W6.1. By contrast the SAME paragraph gives the theme bootstrap two fully mechanical observables ("a structural assertion over the served HTML … and an `addInitScript` capture recording the attribute while `document.readyState === 'loading'`"), showing the story knows how to state a deterministic observable when it has one. `testing-strategy.md` §Rules "No wall-clock ceilings in gated tests": any finite-ms-dependent pass/fail in a gated in-process/browser test is the conditional-test defect class expressed through an assertion value, and the cure is DELETE, not tolerance bands.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Replace the frame assertion with the deterministic pair already proven in the same story: (a) a structural assertion that the identity stylesheet is present in the INITIAL served HTML for the deep-linked identity (the sheet cannot be swapped in later if it shipped correct), and (b) an `addInitScript`/readyState-loading capture of the identity attribute and the resolved role value. If a genuine frame capture is wanted, route it to an on-demand benchmark instrument that reports rather than gates, per the same rule's "a genuinely-owned cost budget belongs in a benchmark instrument".

expertFindings.section: W6.1 — hub verification leg
expertFindings.claim: The hub leg's escape clause has no disposition branch, so the cross-demo exit criterion can be declared met while a hub axis is known-missing. "Any axis found missing is named at the check, never asserted now" states what happens to the finding but not what happens to the gap — and the hub's as-is ruling covers architecture and consumption path, so a missing theme axis has no named owner.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W6.1: "The hub's story is VERIFICATION of its existing wiring with recorded mutation proofs (EX47); any axis found missing is named at the check, never asserted now." §Cross-demo acceptance nonetheless requires "Working theme detection AND selection in every demo". W0.6 shows the correct shape and does it explicitly: "The REMEDIATION BRANCH is explicit (EX32): violations the new suites find are triaged fix-only per ADR-147 … with fix stories named as W0 work".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Mirror W0.6's branch in W6.1: a missing hub axis is triaged fix (a named story minted into the plan body at the check) or recorded exception with the owner's word — never merely named. Otherwise the cross-demo acceptance line is unfalsifiable for one of the four demos.

expertFindings.section: W1.1 / W5.1 — new-workspace plumbing contract ("test naming", vitest base-config pattern)
expertFindings.claim: The plumbing contract lists "vitest base-config pattern, test naming" without resolving either, for two brand-new workspaces. Two concrete consequences: a mis-globbed include passes silently (vitest exits 0 with no discovered tests), and the demos-tier Playwright suffix/location convention stays unstated while the estate's landed idiom (`tests/*.spec.ts`) diverges from the directive's E2E rule.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W1.1: "knip/prettier/markdownlint entries, vitest base-config pattern, test naming, Playwright wired as `test:ui`/`test:a11y`". First-hand the two live demos already disagree: `<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/vitest.config.ts` includes `**/*.{unit,integration}.test.{ts,tsx}` while `<repo>/demos/oak-curriculum-hub/vitest.config.ts` includes `**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` (its tools tests are plain `*.test.ts`). Playwright specs live at `tests/*.spec.ts`, whereas `testing-strategy.md` §Development Workflow states E2E tests live in `e2e-tests/` and MUST end `*.e2e.test.ts`; the only sanctioning precedent is a worked path in `docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md:89`. `testing-tdd-recipes.md` §"Validate Test Discovery" requires `--passWithNoTests=false` wherever a workspace can exit 0 with no discovered tests.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Resolve both in the W0.3 charter ADR (the demos-tier DoD home, which lands before W1.1 opens): state the demos-tier test-naming convention including the browser-suite suffix and directory, and require `--passWithNoTests=false` on each new workspace's `test` script so a naming/glob mismatch fails loudly instead of greening an empty run. The plain demo, which ships almost no unit-testable code, is exactly the workspace where a vacuous vitest leg would go unnoticed.

expertFindings.section: W0.7 — the design-review instrument v0 (fidelity register)
expertFindings.claim: W0.7 "MINTS the fidelity register … as a committed artefact with a stated row schema", but an artefact of that name already exists in the estate with a different schema, a different purpose and its own validator plus tests. The acceptance line "register committed" is satisfiable by the artefact that already exists, and two registers under one name will be confused at every checkpoint that reads one.
expertFindings.evidence: First-hand: `<repo>/demos/oak-curriculum-hub/fidelity-register.json` carries rows shaped `{id, pairId, kind, summary, evidence, disposition: 'deliberate'|'investigate', rationale, author, date}` — export-divergence dispositions, not owner wow verdicts — with `tools/fidelity-register.ts` and `tools/fidelity-register.test.ts` beside it. Plan W0.7's schema is "page, demo, verdict (PASS/FAIL/ITERATE), the qualities judged, owner-statement date".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the new artefact distinctly (e.g. the wow-verdict register) or state explicitly that W0.7 EXTENDS the landed hub register with a new row kind — and in either case name the validator the new schema gets, on the landed `fidelity-register.ts` precedent, so "committed" is not the whole acceptance. §Quality bar 1 makes this register the resolvable record behind every owner-held criterion; it needs the same schema enforcement the existing one has.

expertFindings.section: W3.0 / W3.1 — fixtures-as-parity
expertFindings.claim: "RED: the family's first fixture" does not say the parity fixture is hand-authored ahead of the component, and nothing forbids regenerating it from component output. A regenerated fixture is a snapshot: it passes by construction, ratifies whatever the component emitted, and updates silently on any refactor — zero design value on the describe-vs-audit test.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W3.1: "Describing surface per family: unit tests + the parity file; RED: the family's first fixture." W3.0 restates fixtures-as-parity (EX25) as "a class-selection contract per prop combination, no longer an independent-implementation drift check" — which removes the independent second implementation that previously made the comparison meaningful, leaving the fixture as the sole expectation. `test-immediate-fails.md` item 19 rejects tests that prove the scaffolding rather than product code; `tdd-as-design.md` §Describe vs. Audit names "could be derived mechanically from the product code" as the audit cue.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State in W3.0's mapping-rule contract that parity fixtures are HAND-AUTHORED expectations landed in the same commit as the component (the atomic landing), never emitted from component output, and that any fixture change must travel with the behaviour change that justifies it. Add the mutation check `testing-strategy.md` §"Prove the guard bites" already requires elsewhere in this plan: mutate one prop→class mapping, confirm exactly that family's parity test fails.

expertFindings.section: W0.3 (Demos Charter — composition envelope) and §Relationships (ADR obligations by workstream)
expertFindings.claim: The charter's "composition envelope" forks owner-authored doctrine that already has a canonical home, and the plan never touches ADR-213 §3's composition clause — whose own text names an owner fork that this plan silently steps over.
expertFindings.evidence: grep across <repo>/.agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md and dispositions.v2.1.md for `one-html-many-css`, `composition doctrine`, `region contract` returns nothing (exit 1). But <repo>/docs/governance/one-html-many-css-compositions.md §15 (lines 785–836, practical rules 14–16) already states the same substance the charter would carry: "the canonical HTML should represent a defensible base narrative, while themes should be tested to ensure visual movement does not create a confusing focus path", `reading-flow` "treated as progressive enhancement rather than the sole accessibility mechanism", "Preserve a coherent canonical DOM sequence". Its frontmatter calls it "the repo's durable design-principle home" (owner-authored 2026-07-19). ADR-213 lines 430–434 bind page composition to that doc and add: "The contract currently binds no shipped surface; its first named binding is the hub shell at the hub's convergence lane (until then it is recorded as future-surfaces doctrine — owner fork if that binding should differ)." W1.2/W1.4/W4.2/W5.2 ship composition variants across four demos, so the first named binding becomes the plain demo, not the hub shell — and `ws-hub-migration` (the hub convergence lane) stays owned by the backlog plan.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Home the envelope where the concept already lives: a dated addition to docs/governance/one-html-many-css-compositions.md for the per-variant declared-reading-sequence refinement, with the charter ADR citing it rather than restating it (ADR-127 §5 SSOT). Add an ADR-213 §3 dated amendment to W0.3's acceptance recording that the region contract's first named binding moves from the hub shell to the demos tier, and surface the clause's explicit "owner fork if that binding should differ" as an owner card rather than absorbing it at the seat.

expertFindings.section: W3.0 (ADR-213 §3 dated amendment) and §Relationships
expertFindings.claim: The §3 amendment the plan will land asserts a role for the studio seeds — "fixtures-guarded" — that no story in this plan establishes, that has never landed, and that the same story's landing-sequence set migrates away. Executing W3.0 as written produces a self-contradictory ADR §3.
expertFindings.evidence: W3.0 text: "the studio seeds remain the tier-3 token-sufficiency proof (peer consumption, fixtures-guarded, unchanged in purpose)" and, four sentences later, "The §3 landing-sequence set rides the first component export: ADR-041 map note, `.design-sync/conventions.md` rewrite + re-sync, the fixtures-parity migration (re-homed from `ws-fixtures-parity`…)". <repo>/docs/architecture/architectural-decisions/213-design-system-integration-and-component-architecture.md line 395 (unamended by this plan) reads "fixtures-as-parity migrates from reference-proof duty to the tier package's own tests". <repo>/.agent/plans-backlog-2026-07/architecture-and-infrastructure/current/design-system-integration.plan.md `ws-fixtures-parity` is `status: pending` — the seed-side guard was never built, so there is nothing to migrate and nothing guarding the seeds afterwards. W3.0 further re-scopes fixtures-as-parity to "a class-selection contract per prop combination", i.e. a tier-side check only.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Decide and state which shape the amendment records: either (a) a SPLIT — a named story lands the seed-side token-sufficiency fixtures inside `oak-design-system` and the §3 landing-sequence clause is amended from "migrates" to "splits", with the tier taking the class-selection contract; or (b) drop "fixtures-guarded" from the seeds' described role and say what does guard them. Put the choice in W3.0's acceptance line so the ADR text is decidable at authoring time.

expertFindings.section: §Relationships ("ADR-213 §3's executor pointer updates")
expertFindings.claim: Re-pointing ADR-213 §3's executor pointer at this plan node keeps a permanent doc depending on an ephemeral one — and the replacement target is an unratified sketch. The same plan applies the correct cure (pointer → outcome) to ADR-147/ADR-121, so it contradicts its own doctrine.
expertFindings.evidence: ADR-213 lines 386–388 cite "`ws-gate-extension` in the design-system-integration plan" as the hard gate's executor. The plan's §Relationships says only "ADR-213 §3's executor pointer updates", while W2.5 and the obligations map commit to "replace plan-item pointers with outcomes" for ADR-147/ADR-121 (EX62). <repo>/agent-tools/src/validators/reference-direction/validate-reference-direction.ts polices `docs/architecture/architectural-decisions` as a source and classifies `.agent/plans/` as ephemeral, exiting 1 (BLOCKING, wired into `repo-validators:check`) on any markdown-link reference — so writing the new pointer as a link fails `pnpm check`, and writing it in backticks only evades the gate. The target node carries `status: sketch`, `ratified_by: null`.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: In the same amendment, state the OUTCOME in ADR-213 §3 (the gate extension's substance as the ship condition for the first component export) and delete the plan-name pointer entirely; record the carrier (W2.10) in the plan body only — identical to the cure W2.5 applies to ADR-147/ADR-121.

expertFindings.section: W0.3 (The Demos Charter as doctrine)
expertFindings.claim: The charter is specified as an implementation runbook, which PDR-019's WHAT-not-HOW discipline forbids for new ADRs.
expertFindings.evidence: W0.3 loads the ADR with: "the per-demo pre-paint mechanism (raw inline head script for the Next demos; parser-blocking `<script src>` in `<head>` for the plain demo)"; "SC 2.4.11 with a concrete cell (tab through every page with the switchboard sticky; the focused element's rect never fully covered)"; "`reading-flow` rides as progressive enhancement per variant". <repo>/.agent/practice-core/decision-records/PDR-019-adr-scope-by-reusability.md §"ADRs state WHAT, not HOW": the Decision section records "the choice made; the scope of the choice" and NOT "implementation steps; code snippets…; configuration values that will drift", with implementation belonging to "plan bodies" and "runbooks and READMEs"; the discipline "applies to new ADRs authored after the 2026-04-21 amendment date".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Keep in the ADR: the demo-assignment decision with its provenance note, the as-is scope rule, the three-identities reading, the DoD-is-a-floor stance, and the composition-envelope principle by reference. Move the pre-paint mechanisms, the concrete Playwright cells, and the `reading-flow` technique into the plan body and each demo's README/DoD, which W0.3 is already editing.

expertFindings.section: W0.3 (correction set — `demos/README.md`)
expertFindings.claim: The prescribed edit puts a second copy of the assignment table in demos/README.md while the clause's own parenthetical claims "one home per fact", and it leaves two existing authority statements in that README unreconciled.
expertFindings.evidence: W0.3: the ADR "carries: the assignment table (hub = … showcase = … plain = … styled = …)" AND "`demos/README.md` — ADD a §Charter section (pointer + row-per-demo table) … (EX59/EX76: no §Charter exists today; one home per fact)". <repo>/demos/README.md lines 6–13 already state the tier's standards ("strict TypeScript, the full shared ESLint ruleset, TDD, and WCAG 2.2 AA") and declare "The root gate configs … are authoritative for the current gate footprint over this tier", plus "the productionisation roadmap is owned by productionisation-and-reuse.plan.md" — which the EX71 re-homing partly invalidates.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make the README §Charter a pointer plus per-demo links only (no row-per-demo restatement of the assignment). In the same edit, reconcile the "root gate configs are authoritative" sentence with the charter's DoD-floor claim, and true the productionisation-plan ownership sentence to the re-homing.

expertFindings.section: W0.3 acceptance / D1 sequencing
expertFindings.claim: The correction set re-describes workspaces before the code changes, so the landed docs assert a state that stays false for most of the plan.
expertFindings.evidence: D1 puts the charter merge "before W1.1 opens"; W0.3's acceptance is "ADR landed, README edits in place, citations resolve", and the correction set includes "showcase README + `package.json` description". Today <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/package.json reads "plain-CSS kit consumption with identity and theme switching" and its README line 5 reads "plain-CSS kit consumption — no Tailwind, no PostCSS, no mapping layer". The showcase is not rebuilt as React+Tailwind until W4.2 and the plain demo does not exist until W1.1.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split the correction set by artefact kind: the ADR and demos/README.md's §Charter pointer land at W0.3 (a decision may precede its implementation); each workspace's own README and `package.json` description edit becomes an acceptance line on that workspace's landing PR (W1.1, W4.2, W5.1), where it describes something true.

expertFindings.section: W0.3 acceptance (`check:docs` + the estate validator)
expertFindings.claim: The new charter ADR has no obligation to appear in the ADR index, and no gate would catch its absence.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/docs/architecture/architectural-decisions/README.md §"Creating an ADR": "Number sequentially from the highest existing ADR. Add the new entry to the Index above" (highest indexed is ADR-221). `check:docs` resolves to `format-check:root && markdownlint-check:root && docs-validators:check`, i.e. validate-reference-direction / no-machine-local-paths / markdown-links / patterns-index / ratified-lists — none checks ADR-index membership (verified: no validator source under agent-tools/src references the ADR directory for index coverage). The plan never mentions the ADR index (grep for `index`/`architectural-decisions` in the plan body returns only citation-legend hits).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add the index entry (number + one-line summary, sequential from the highest existing ADR) to W0.3's acceptance line alongside the ADR-213 one-line pointer amendment, so the charter is reachable through the stable index (ADR-127 §5).

expertFindings.section: §Relationships (ADR obligations by workstream)
expertFindings.claim: The obligations map enumerates ADR amendments meticulously but omits the two governance docs that are the durable homes for the practice W2 changes, so both go stale silently.
expertFindings.evidence: The plan's only governance reference is a single DoD pointer to `docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md` (line 238). <repo>/docs/governance/design-token-practice.md self-describes as "the durable reference that workspace READMEs and reviewer reading requirements link to", and enumerates the theme-selection mechanics (`:root:not([data-theme='light'])` plus `[data-theme]`) and the four-theme AA/AAA gate state — all of which W2.1/W2.4 change (orthogonal contrast/colour-vision axes, `html:not([data-theme])` scoping, identity-authored base+overlay trees). ADR-147 §Rule scoping names accessibility-practice.md as the home of the forced-colours worked instance, which W2.1's forced-colours adaptation block extends.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add both to the by-workstream obligations with acceptance lines: W2.1/W2.4 → dated amendment to design-token-practice.md (identity-authored trees, the axis model, the selector set); W2.1/W2.5 → dated addition to accessibility-practice.md (forced-colours adaptation obligations and the demos-tier SC additions), with the charter pointing at that home instead of carrying its own copy.

expertFindings.section: W2 preamble / obligations map (ADR-213 §2 + §4 amendments)
expertFindings.claim: The identity-as-configuration architecture is landed as amendments to ADR-213 §2/§4, growing an already-overloaded ADR, while the plan mints a separate ADR for the strictly smaller demos-charter decision — an inconsistent application of the same doctrine it cites.
expertFindings.evidence: ADR-213 is 531 lines and already carries four stacked dated §2 amendment blocks (2026-07-19, 2026-07-20 ×2, 2026-07-20 slot (c)) plus two §3 amendments. The new decision set — a JSON-Schema identity manifest, per-theme overlay trees, a value-free identity CSS layer, an emitter, a new `packages/design/` workspace, the Oak projection asymmetry — is a first-order architecture with rejected alternatives, exactly PDR-019's ADR-worthy profile. The plan's own EX60 rationale for the charter is "curing the god-document and SSOT-fork costs" (ADR-127 §5 single responsibility).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Mint one "identity as configuration" ADR (manifest + emitter + identity layer + the Oak asymmetry + rejected alternatives), and reduce ADR-213 §2/§4 to one-line dated pointer amendments — the same shape W0.3 uses for the charter. Re-point W2.0/W2.1/W2.2's acceptance lines at the new ADR.

expertFindings.section: W2 preamble ("the dated ADR-213 §2 amendment records exactly this split")
expertFindings.claim: The §2 amendment as scoped does not say how §2's CSS-is-the-token-source invariant binds non-Oak identities, whose token trees are authored and whose CSS is generated — the inverse direction.
expertFindings.evidence: ADR-213 §2: "The design system's CSS is the token source of truth; DTCG JSON trees are a generated interchange projection of it", preserving ADR-148's invariant that "secondary outputs are projections of the token source, never a parallel token system". The plan's W2/W2.1: "non-Oak identities author their token blocks" as base + per-theme overlay trees, from which W2.2's emitter generates brand CSS. The plan's amendment description covers only the Oak clause ("No Oak token is ever authored twice").
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Scope the invariant explicitly in the amendment (or the new identity ADR): CSS-is-source binds the kit/Oak token layer; per non-Oak identity the authored manifest + trees are the source and the emitted brand CSS is its projection; state which artefact wins if an identity's emitted CSS is hand-edited, so a later reader cannot misread an authored Freedonia tree as a §2 violation.

expertFindings.section: W2.4 (theme-control surface flag) vs W1.2/W1.3/W1.5 and §Quality bar
expertFindings.claim: Director constraint EX28(4) — flag the theme-control surface implication to the wow checkpoints — is implemented only inside W2.4, which runs after the first two owner checkpoints that render a theme control. The flag cannot inform the checkpoints it was ruled for.
expertFindings.evidence: W2.4: "The THEME-CONTROL SURFACE implication of the axis model (a two-axis control, or composed presets) is FLAGGED in the wow-checkpoint notes wherever a theme control renders … no separate pre-emptive gate (Director ruling, 2026-08-02)." W1.2 specifies the control concretely ("a toggle-button group in each page's masthead … wired to `oak-theme.js` `set()`"), and W1.3/W1.5 are `owner-held` checkpoints. §Sequencing: "W0 → W1 (first light ×2) → W2 ∥ W3". §Quality bar items 1–5 carry no such note.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Carry the flag in §Quality bar as a standing checkpoint note and in W1.2's control spec, so the W1.3 sitting prices the axis-model implication on the first rendered control; state in W1.2 or W2.4 whether the W1 control is re-faced to the owner after W2.4 lands, so the rework is visible rather than discovered.

expertFindings.section: W0.6 / W2.5 (ADR-147 §Standard + ADR-121 matrix amendments)
expertFindings.claim: The stale-CI truing is bound to W2.5, but the first story that lands new CI-run a11y suites is W0.6 — so both ADRs stay false through all of W0 and W1 while the plan is actively adding to the surface they misdescribe.
expertFindings.evidence: ADR-147 §Tooling: "Currently enforced in `pnpm check` (local); promotion to pre-push and CI is tracked in the quality gate hardening plan (item 0d)"; ADR-121 line 69's matrix already records `test:a11y` CI = Yes while lines 89–92 and 207 still say it is pnpm-check-only and cite "the quality gate hardening plan (item 0d)". <repo>/.github/workflows/ci.yml line 230 runs `test:e2e test:ui test:a11y test:widget`. W0.6 wires the new hub suites "as `test:ui`/`test:a11y` so turbo and CI run them"; the amendment sits in W2.5.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Move the ADR-147 §Tooling / ADR-121 matrix truing (state the landed CI position as an outcome; delete the plan-item pointer) to W0.6's acceptance — the first story that touches that surface — and leave W2.5 with only the §Standard theme-cardinality and coverage-matrix additions it actually introduces.

expertFindings.section: §Relationships ("Strategic node companion edit")
expertFindings.claim: Two-thirds of the stated companion edit already landed; the row describes completed work as riding this node's landing change, making that acceptance line a no-op.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/.agent/plans/strategic/design-system-as-configured-framework.plan.md is committed (last touched in e3574388b) and already carries `serves: TOOLS-2` (line 10) plus the APP-1 prose and "(Serves edge re-pointed APP-1 → TOOLS-2, 2026-08-02, v1-review finding E65…)" (lines 41–43). Only the report-path on that citation is outstanding.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Narrow the row to the one outstanding edit (add the `.agent/reports/design/plan-review-2026-08-02/` path to the E65 citation per the legend convention) and drop the already-landed `serves` re-point from the landing change's acceptance.

expertFindings.section: W0.3 correction set
expertFindings.claim: The correction set is a hand list, and it is already both inaccurate and incomplete against the surfaces that carry the superseded showcase description.
expertFindings.evidence: `docs/consuming-nextjs.md` does not resolve from the repo root; the file is <repo>/packages/design/oak-design-system/docs/consuming-nextjs.md (verified by find). Surfaces carrying "plain-CSS" that the set omits: <repo>/pnpm-workspace.yaml line 8 ("# Demo: one-page design-system showcase (plain-CSS kit consumption)."), demos/oak-design-showcase/app/globals.css line 2, demos/oak-design-showcase/components/Hero.tsx line 10.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Qualify the consuming-nextjs path to its workspace, add the pnpm-workspace.yaml comment to the set, and note that the globals.css header and Hero copy are retired by the W4.2 landing — or derive the set mechanically (grep for the superseded description) rather than hand-listing it, which is the same failure mode EX59 cured for demos/README.md.

expertFindings.section: W0.8 Shared instruments re-homed — clause (c), the shared demos test harness
expertFindings.claim: W0.8 names `packages/core/oak-eslint/scripts/` as the home for the hoisted demos test harness (origin gate, cross-origin interception, apply-state). That home cannot hold it without breaking ADR-041's core row and the package's own surface contract, so the story as written is unexecutable.
expertFindings.evidence: `<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/apply-state.ts` (the named apply-state harness) imports `@axe-core/playwright`, `@playwright/test`, `@oaknational/oak-design-react` and `../tools/showcase-origin`. ADR-041's matrix row `core` sets the `design` cell to `no` ('No monorepo dependencies outside core; external deps must stay minimal and provider-neutral'), so a core-tier file importing `@oaknational/oak-design-react` is a direct violation. `<repo>/packages/core/oak-eslint/package.json` declares `"files": ["dist"]` and `"exports": { ".": ... }` only — there is no subpath under which a demo could import `scripts/*`, and `coreBoundaryRules` sets `import-x/no-relative-packages: 'error'`, so the relative route is closed too. Separately, `validate-boundaries.ts` is the sole current occupant of that scripts dir and is invoked by path (`"validate-boundaries": "cd ../../.. && pnpm exec tsx packages/core/oak-eslint/scripts/validate-boundaries.ts"`), a mechanism a Playwright-imported harness cannot use.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split W0.8: keep (a)/(b) — path-invoked node validators — wherever the seat homes repo validators, but give (c) its own home. The harness is a design-tier-consuming, Playwright-dependent test-support surface; it needs a workspace whose ADR-041 row permits `design` outbound (a new `packages/design/` test-support member, or a new tier row added by the same amendment), with a real `exports` entry and `@playwright/test`/`@axe-core/playwright` as its own deps. Also note in the story that the root `repo-validators:check` chain currently filters `@oaknational/oak-design-showcase validate-authored-css` / `validate-kit-assets` and must be re-pointed in the same PR.

expertFindings.section: W0.8 clause (a) — authored-CSS literal walker, roster widened to the identity directories
expertFindings.claim: W0.8 is sequenced before W1, but its widened walker roster ('derived from the workspace inventory AND including the identity directories') is red against the repository's existing sanctioned state. Its acceptance line — 'validators green over all demos' — is unachievable until W2.2, two workstreams later.
expertFindings.evidence: Running the landed classifier `demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/css-literal-values.ts` first-hand: `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/app/globals.css` → 5 findings; `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/whitelabel/freedonia/brand-full.css` → 59; `demos/oak-design-showcase/public/brands/creature/brand.css` → 71. The identity sheets are value-bearing by construction and only become value-free at W2.2 ('Existing non-`:root` identity CSS is re-expressed … or lands in the value-free identity layer'). The current walker deliberately excludes `public/` with a stated ground ('public/ holds kit-authored copies — definitions, not authored consumption, owned by validate-kit-assets', `demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/validate-authored-css.ts`), and the hub sits under an as-is ruling whose debt this plan records as accepted.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the roster's inclusion rule as a function of migration state, not of directory membership: the identity leg covers the W2.0 home's identity layers only (which do not exist until W2.0), and joins per identity at that identity's W2.2 migration landing. Move the identity leg's acceptance out of W0.8 into W2.2, keep W0.8's non-vacuity leg satisfied by the surfaces that are already clean, and say explicitly whether the hub's authored CSS is in or out of the roster given its as-is ruling.

expertFindings.section: W2.0 The identity-data home / W2.2 The identity emitter
expertFindings.claim: The emitter design inverts the design-tier dependency direction and then claims the inversion is proven safe by a boundary rule that cannot observe it. `design-tokens-core` is the tier member forbidden every sibling import, yet the plan has it consume a sibling workspace's data at build time; 'a file read, never an import edge' is the evasion, not the compliance.
expertFindings.evidence: W2's preamble assigns the emitter mechanism to `design-tokens-core`; W2.0 states 'The emitter reads this workspace at BUILD time — a file read, never an import edge; the boundary rule that proves it is part of this story.' `packages/core/oak-eslint/src/rules/boundary.ts` `createDesignBoundaryRules('design-tokens-core')` restricts all five siblings in both specifier and path-zone form — an ESLint import rule, blind to `fs` reads by construction, so it can prove nothing about this coupling. The plan never names which workspace's build task invokes the emitter, nor any turbo `dependsOn`/`inputs`/`outputs` edge for it, while `turbo.json` shows the estate's established discipline for exactly this class (e.g. the MCP app's `#build` enumerates `$TURBO_ROOT$/packages/design/oak-design-system/**` inputs and `public/oak-ds/**` outputs for a build-time copy).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Invert the invocation: the W2.0 identity workspace owns the emit task and imports the emitter mechanism from `design-tokens-core` (an upward, lint-visible, ADR-041-legal edge), with manifest paths and output targets passed as parameters per ADR-024 rather than resolved inside the mechanism. Make the emitter's turbo task an explicit acceptance line (task name, `dependsOn`, `inputs`, `outputs`) so every downstream consumer's build orders behind it.

expertFindings.section: W2.2 The Oak asymmetry / W2.6 Standing falsifiers vs the strategic node's §Falsifiability
expertFindings.claim: The Oak asymmetry institutionalises a per-identity branch inside the framework, and the standing falsifier is designed so it can never exercise that branch — so the strategic node's own falsification test passes vacuously while the thesis it tests is weakened.
expertFindings.evidence: The strategic node `<repo>/.agent/plans/strategic/design-system-as-configured-framework.plan.md` states: 'The thesis fails if adding or modifying an identity requires framework-code changes (the identity-№N test)'. W2.2 gives Oak a dedicated CSS→DTCG projection generator ('Oak authors no manifest token block'; 'non-Oak identities author their token blocks'), i.e. one identity's token data arrives via bespoke framework code. W2.6(a)'s synthetic identity fixture is 'a synthetic identity fixture in a fixture-manifest directory', which exercises the authored-manifest path only; the Oak generator path has no №N cell.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Recast the generator as a general input adapter — an identity's token block may be supplied as an authored tree OR derived from a declared CSS source, chosen by a manifest field — so Oak is a configuration selection rather than a code branch. Add a falsifier cell that mints identity №N through the CSS-derived input path, so both input shapes are covered by the standing test rather than one.

expertFindings.section: W2.3 Theme roster generation / W3.3 Identity runtime binding / §Relationships ADR obligations map
expertFindings.claim: Two new relations touch the kit — generated source emitted into it, and a new runtime module added beside `oak-theme.js` — but the obligations map carries no ADR amendment for either, and W2's own preamble asserts the opposite ('the kit's public surface unchanged').
expertFindings.evidence: W2.3: 'the kit runtime's union and the tier's type file are EMIT-INTO-CONSUMER codegen outputs'. W3.3: '`oakIdentity` beside `oak-theme.js` … owned by the kit workspace'. ADR-213 §4 enumerates the kit's surface as a closed list — 'its public surface is built CSS, the theme-switcher JS (`oak-theme.js`), plus the generated DTCG export artefact' — and states 'oak-design-system has zero runtime monorepo dependencies'. §Relationships' 'ADR obligations by workstream' lists W0.3, W1.1/W5.1, W2.0, W2.1, W2.2, W2.5, W3.0, W6.3 — no W2.3, no W3.3. `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` also fences `oak-theme.js` by name ('packages/design/oak-design-system/(src/)?oak-theme\\.(ts|js)$'), so a second browser entry script needs its own entry.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add to the obligations map: W2.3 → a dated ADR-213 §4 amendment recording the codegen-into-consumer relation (which workspace writes, which files are generated, how drift is gated) alongside the unchanged no-runtime-import invariant; W3.3 → a dated ADR-213 §4 amendment extending the kit's enumerated public surface to the identity runtime. Correct the W2 preamble sentence, which the plan's own W3.3 contradicts.

expertFindings.section: W2.3 — the mechanical consumer-census validator
expertFindings.claim: The validator as specified ('fails any literal theme-name roster outside the generated module + the pinned expectations module — repo-wide') fires on the estate's sanctioned byte-parity copies of the theme runtime, so it lands red or needs an exemption set the plan never states.
expertFindings.evidence: The five-name roster is literal in `packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:31`, in the committed root `packages/design/oak-design-system/oak-theme.js`, and in both served copies `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/public/oak-theme.js` and `demos/oak-design-showcase/public/oak-theme.js` (each confirmed by grep). Those copies are sanctioned duplicates: `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` excludes them by name with the ground 'byte-parity with the package is test-enforced'. Two more demos add two more copies. Further literal rosters exist at `demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/apply-state.ts` (`PALETTE_THEMES`) and `apps/oak-curriculum-mcp-streamable-http/tests/visual/apply-theme.ts` (`THEMES`).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the validator's allow-set explicitly in W2.3: the generated module, the pinned expectations module, and the byte-parity served copies of the kit runtime (which are outputs of the generated module, not independent rosters, and are already parity-gated). Name the parity gate as the mechanism that discharges the copies, so the census check and the parity check compose rather than contradict.

expertFindings.section: W1.1 / W5.1 — the new-workspace plumbing contract
expertFindings.claim: The plumbing contract is presented as complete but omits the turbo task registration every existing demo carries, so the styled-components demo would land outside the estate's caching and invalidation contract while its acceptance line ('`pnpm check` green from cold') still passes.
expertFindings.evidence: `turbo.json` carries three explicit per-workspace overrides for each existing demo — `@oaknational/oak-curriculum-hub#build|#type-check|#lint` and `@oaknational/oak-design-showcase#build|#type-check|#lint` — each setting `"outputs": [".next/**", "!.next/cache/**"]` and `"inputs": [..., "!.next/**", ...]`. The root `build` task's outputs are `dist/**`/`.tsup/**` only, so a Next demo without its override produces uncached output and hashes its own `.next` tree as input. The W1.1 contract enumerates pnpm-workspace registration, the ADR-041 amendment, the validate-boundaries leg, depcruise rules, knip/prettier/markdownlint, vitest config, test naming, Playwright scripts, the shared harness, and kit-copy parity — turbo appears nowhere in the plan except once, at W0.6, about test scripts.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add to the W1.1/W5.1 contract: the per-workspace turbo task entries (`#build`/`#type-check`/`#lint` with outputs and input exclusions, mirroring the landed demos), and the `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` exclusion entry for each new demo's served `public/oak-theme.js` copy — both are per-demo obligations the landed estate already demonstrates.

expertFindings.section: W2.2 / W4.4 / §Out of scope — the second Oak token projection
expertFindings.claim: W2.2 mints a generated Oak DTCG projection while the imported `dtcg/` trees remain the landed four-theme gate's input, and §Out of scope leaves Stage B convergence owned by another plan — so the plan lands a second Oak token projection with no stated convergence owner, which is the parallel-token-system shape ADR-148/ADR-213 §2 exists to forbid.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/` contains the imported trees (`palette.json`, `primitives.json`, `semantic.{light,dark,high-contrast,colour-safe}.json`, `contrast-pairings.json` with 42 pairs, verified) and the kit has no generation script (`package.json` scripts: build, build:flat, clean, sync:runtime, type-check, test, lint). ADR-213 §2: 'DTCG JSON trees are a generated interchange projection of it … never a parallel token system', with Stage B as the single atomic switch. This plan's §Out of scope: 'Stage B token-source convergence and the dual-gate window's closure (owned by `design-system-integration` `ws-stage-b-convergence`)', while W2.2 claims to be 'discharging ADR-213 §2's existing regenerated-export obligation'.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State in W2.2 what happens to the imported `dtcg/` trees and the landed four-theme gate's input at the moment the generated Oak projection lands: either the generator becomes that gate's input in the same change (and the §2 amendment records the retirement), or the generated projection is scoped explicitly as identity-gate-only with a named convergence obligation carried into `ws-stage-b-convergence` by the same dated amendment that re-homes the other three workstreams.

expertFindings.section: §Relationships — Strategic node companion edit
expertFindings.claim: The plan describes an act as riding its landing change that has already landed, re-introducing the false-repository-claim class the §Review record declares extinct for round 2.
expertFindings.evidence: §Relationships: 'Strategic node companion edit: `design-system-as-configured-framework` re-points `serves` to TOOLS-2 with APP-1 named in prose, and its review citation gains the report path per the legend convention (EX64) — rides this node's landing change.' On disk, `<repo>/.agent/plans/strategic/design-system-as-configured-framework.plan.md` already carries `serves: TOOLS-2` and the APP-1 prose; `git diff HEAD` on that path is empty and `git log` shows it landed in `e3574388b`. Only the citation-path half is genuinely outstanding (the node's citation reads 'v1-review finding E65' with no report path).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Reduce the row to what remains true: the serves re-point landed at `e3574388b` (dated fact); the outstanding companion edit is the citation's report path per the legend convention. Re-run the same check over the other §Relationships rows that describe amendments as pending.

expertFindings.section: W1.1 — the ADR-041 demos amendment (EX73)
expertFindings.claim: The amendment as specified adds a demos ROW to a matrix that is row/column symmetric, leaving eight existing rows with no demos cell and the inbound rule unrecorded where the ADR is authoritative — and it leaves standing a sentence the same PR falsifies.
expertFindings.evidence: `docs/architecture/architectural-decisions/041-workspace-structure-option-a.md`'s matrix header is `| Importer | core | foundation libs | adapter libs | sdks | design | apps | agent-tools | agent-graphs | Constraint |` — eight importee columns against eight importer rows, and the ADR's own consequences text asserts that shape ('the dependency-direction matrix now records eight importer rows and eight importee columns'). The `demos/` bullet currently reads 'Recorded intent: never imported by packages — no boundary rule enforces the inbound direction yet; enforcement lands at need', which W1.1's `no-packages-to-demos` depcruise rule makes false in the same change. The plan's W1.1 names only 'the demos matrix row (outbound allowances enumerated)'.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Specify the amendment as row AND column: add the demos importee column with `no` in every existing row (the inbound rule, recorded where the matrix is authoritative), and true the `demos/` bullet to name the landed depcruise rule as its enforcement. Also reconsider enumerating `foundation libs`/`adapter libs` as `yes` for demos — no demo consumes either today (hub and showcase deps are core, sdks, design only), so those cells widen the boundary ahead of any consumer.

expertFindings.section: W2.0 acceptance lines / W2.8 Identity asset delivery
expertFindings.claim: W2.0's acceptance under-scopes the boundary work a new design workspace requires, and neither W2.0 nor W2.8 states any relationship to the existing `oak-design-assets` workspace whose purpose the new home overlaps.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/core/oak-eslint/src/rules/design-boundary.unit.test.ts` enforces pairwise completeness: a `MEMBERS` tuple, an `ALLOWED_EDGES` map, an inventory-parity case, and `it.each(MEMBERS)('restricts %s from every non-edge design package in both forms')`. A sixth rule-building member therefore requires edits to all five existing `createDesignBoundaryRules` branches plus both test tables — not just 'the `DESIGN_PACKAGE_IMPORTS` entry, the `createDesignBoundaryRules` branch' the story names. Separately, `packages/design/oak-design-assets/package.json` describes itself as 'Oak brand raster artwork — the assets that must be files rather than tokens or CSS, held once for every surface that needs them' and holds `assets/oak-national-academy-logo-512.png`, while W2.8 vendors 'icons + logo' per identity into the W2.0 home.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Extend W2.0's acceptance to name the five sibling-branch updates and the two test tables. Add a sentence to W2.8 dispositioning `oak-design-assets`: either it becomes Oak's identity payload location (and the W2.0 home references it), or it is absorbed and retired at Oak's migration landing — 'held once for every surface' cannot survive two asset homes unstated.

expertFindings.section: W5.3 Consumption through the tier
expertFindings.claim: The stated warrant for the story — that the styled demo is the tier's second consumer — is false against the repository, which weakens the consolidate-at-second-consumer argument the plan leans on.
expertFindings.evidence: `@oaknational/oak-design-react` already has two consumers: `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/package.json` and `demos/oak-design-showcase/package.json` both declare it, and both import it — `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx:15` and `components/framework/LearningFramework.tsx:6` import `oakThemeStore`; `demos/oak-design-showcase/components/Switchboard.tsx:32` does the same; `demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/apply-state.ts:18` imports `OakThemeName` from it.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Reword to what is true and load-bearing: the styled demo is the second consumer of the tier's COMPONENT surface (the theme-store adapter already has two). That is the claim the thinness proof actually needs, and it keeps the second-consumer trigger honest.

expertFindings.section: W2.5(iii) state-matrix specimen carrier / W2.6(a) synthetic identity fixture route
expertFindings.claim: Two load-bearing test surfaces are specified as 'test-only fixture routes … excluded from shipped builds' with no owning workspace named for one and no exclusion mechanism named for either — in App Router demos, a route under `app/` ships by default.
expertFindings.evidence: W2.5(iii) requires 'a state-matrix specimen carrier per identity × theme … a TEST-ONLY fixture route' and W2.5's acceptance is 'matrix wired into `pnpm check`; cell count pinned' — but no workspace is named as the carrier's home, while W2.6(a) places its fixture 'demos-tier, excluded from shipped builds and the W4.5 demonstrating-surface set'. Both existing demos are Next App Router apps (`next: 16.2.11` in both `package.json`s) with `test:ui`/`test:a11y` Playwright scripts, and the repository shows no precedent for a build-excluded route.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the owning workspace for the W2.5 carrier and state the exclusion mechanism concretely for both (a route group behind an env-gated `generateStaticParams`/route-segment guard, a separate fixture app, or a Playwright-served static fixture outside `app/`), plus the assertion that proves the exclusion holds in a production build — otherwise 'excluded from shipped builds' is an unverified property in an acceptance line.

frameFindings.claim: Counter-identity wow has no taste anchor and is discovered at maximum sunk cost: the plan's entire design-excellence source is the Oak export, yet two of the three identities the showcase must render at all times have no analogous anchor, no direction-setting moment, and no early look — their first wow signal arrives in W2.9, AFTER the full W2 machinery spend (schema, emitter, roster, overlays, gate matrix, assets).
frameFindings.evidence: W0.7 derives rubric criteria 'from the export's own design language' and §Direction states 'The export's visual language is the demonstrated taste anchor' — both are Oak's language. W2.9 ('Deliberate visual authorship of EMC² and Freedonia's config values') is the sole design-authorship story for two whole identities, its carrier is per-identity static builds of emitted config (requires W2.1/W2.2), and it asserts 'Each identity passes the W0.7 instrument in its own right' — i.e. counter-identity excellence is adjudicated by an Oak-derived rubric, which measures conformance to Oak's grammar, not excellence in EMC²'s or Freedonia's own voice. Meanwhile both identities render TODAY (W0.4 verifies their live brand.css first-hand), so a zero-cost pre-read exists — the exact FR6 logic the plan applied to the hub (W0.9) and to nobody else. This replicates the v1/v2 failure pattern one level up: identity machinery before counter-identity pixels.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Mint a W0/W1 counter-identity pre-read (serve the existing EMC² and Freedonia renders, owner browses, verdicts in the fidelity register — symmetric with W0.9) plus one owner direction sitting per counter-identity that mints each identity's own taste anchor BEFORE W2 opens; the W0.7 rubric gains per-identity language sections at that sitting, so W2.9's instrument pass judges each identity against its own anchor.

frameFindings.claim: The design-review instrument is structurally the author judging their own work: the only pre-owner filter on every render is the authoring seat applying a seat-authored rubric, with accessibility as the sole paired expert leg — so the plan can pass every gate while the owner remains the first and only design-literate eye, the exact failure mode that produced the rejected v1 showcase page.
frameFindings.evidence: W0.7: the rubric is 'applied manually side-by-side at every checkpoint by the seat + the paired accessibility-expert review leg' — no independent design reviewer exists anywhere in the pre-render path (Quality bar 2: 'the W0.7 rubric + accessibility-expert leg run BEFORE any render is shown'). The graded calibration corpus (export must-pass, degraded-export mutations must-fail) catches degradations of known-good pages, but the actual wow failure mode is 'competent but flat' novel composition — which the author, who already believed the page satisfied the criteria, will score as passing. The plan itself concedes the instrument's authority is unearned at first use ('its miss rate against the owner's actual verdicts is recorded so its blocking authority is earned') — meaning the owner's sittings absorb every early miss. The estate has a standing invoke-design-system-expert rule and an Opus-reviewer doctrine; the plan uses neither for visual judgement.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Add an independent fresh-context design-expert review leg (Opus, per the estate's reviewer doctrine and invoke-design-system-expert rule) to W0.7's pre-render pass alongside the accessibility leg, judging renders against the rubric AND free-form; its verdicts join the miss-rate record so both instruments earn authority against the owner's eye.

frameFindings.claim: Wow-verdict coverage over the identity × theme matrix is unspecified and non-default themes have no design-authorship story: dark, high-contrast, and colour-safe are engineered (W2.4 overlay re-architecture) and mechanically gated (W2.5 contrast/a11y), but nobody authors them to the bar, and nothing states which cells an owner PASS covers — so a demo can clear every checkpoint shown in Oak-light while its dark/HC/colour-safe renders are gate-compliant and visually mediocre.
frameFindings.evidence: The Quality bar (items 1–5) and the fidelity-register schema (page, demo, verdict, qualities, date) never name identity/theme cells; §Cross-demo acceptance requires HC and colour-safe merely 'reachable from the visible theme control'. W2.4 is a re-plumbing story (palette-slot references, axis composition) with acceptance 'each identity renders its OWN high-contrast and colour-safe palettes… gate-proven per W2.5' — contrast ratios, not design quality. This is precisely the 'pass every gate while the demos still look mediocre' shape: contrast gates are satisfiable by ugly palettes.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: The fidelity-register row schema gains a cells-covered field; each whole-demo checkpoint (W4.7/W5.5/W6.2) names a minimum owner-viewed cell set (every identity × both polarities, plus HC and colour-safe at least once per demo); W2.4's acceptance adds a W0.7 instrument pass on the re-authored non-default themes, and W2.9 explicitly covers each counter-identity's full theme roster, not just its default.

frameFindings.claim: The census disposition vocabulary quietly converts the owner's verbatim 'ALL pages from the design system export' into a seat design decision: `fold-into-composition` and `reference-tier` dispositions let export pages not appear as pages with no owner word — only `owner-accepted-exclusion` requires his word.
frameFindings.evidence: W0.1 dispositions page-census rows as 'express-composed / fold-into-composition / reference-tier / owner-accepted-exclusion'; FR2 (applied in W1.4) makes fold decisions 'design decisions, never mechanical census assignments' adjudicated by the W0.7 instrument — i.e. by the seat. The owner will not enumerate ~79 pages by eye at a whole-demo browse, so a folded page's absence is invisible at every checkpoint. The owner's requirement was per-page ('including all pages from the design system export'); the plan's mechanism guards per-feature coverage (W4.5) but lets per-page presence be traded away below his word.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: For PAGE-census rows (as distinct from feature rows), any disposition other than express-composed requires owner word — either fold the fold/reference page decisions into one batched owner card at W1.4's page-set finalisation (the artefact already exists and is final before W4.2), or restrict page-row dispositions to express / owner-accepted-exclusion.

frameFindings.claim: First light is still gated on a plumbing tranche that contradicts the probe's own stated purpose: W1 waits on six W0 stories including full census mechanisation (bidirectional fixture tests, parity counts), the charter ADR merged through review, and the W0.8 validator/harness re-homing — none of which the three plain pages or the two showcase probe pages need — so every gating story raises the sunk cost of exactly the taste discovery W1.5 exists to make cheap.
frameFindings.evidence: 'W1 needs only the named W0 stories (W0.1 census, W0.2(a)/(b) stabilise, W0.3 charter, W0.7 instrument v0, W0.8 re-homes, W0.9 hub pre-read)' and W0.3: 'the ADR merges before W1.1 opens (D1)'. Yet W1.5's own text claims the wow unknown 'is discovered at MINIMUM sunk cost', and the probe runs 'IN the existing showcase workspace against kit classes' — needing no census generator (the export's composed pages are known by inspection; the plan's own dated evidence records the 79-page count first-hand already), no charter ADR, and no re-homed harness. The owner's ruling is 'never workstreams of plumbing before pixels'; W0 minus stabilise/pre-read/rubric is a workstream of plumbing before pixels.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Split the W1 gate: W1.5 (showcase probe) and a provisional W1.2 render gate only on W0.2(a) stabilise, W0.7's v0 rubric, and W0.9; W0.1's mechanised census, the charter ADR, and W0.8's re-homing proceed in parallel and gate the W1.1/W5.1 workspace landings and W4 — not the first pixels in front of the owner.

frameFindings.claim: The owner's export tweak list — his own words: 'it has tweaks that I need made' — stays unenumerated until entries passively arrive, so first light can render export pages the owner already wants changed, spending wow checkpoint #1 on known-stale pixels and souring the first wow.
frameFindings.evidence: W0.5 builds an intake SURFACE (design-sync NOTES, read at workstream opens, confirmed at W1.3) but no story ever asks the owner to enumerate the list he already holds; W1.2 authors the export's three composed pages fresh before the intake is even confirmed (confirmation is AT W1.3, the checkpoint after authoring). The cheapest de-risk in the whole plan — one enumeration sitting — is missing, while the plan spends heavily on the auto-promotion machinery for tweaks arriving later.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Add a tweak-enumeration sitting to W0.5 (owner lists known tweaks once, each entry dated with his blocking/non-blocking word), sequenced before W1.2 page selection; blocking tweaks touching the three chosen pages land in the W1.2 authoring itself.

frameFindings.claim: The styled demo's visual differentiation is asserted at checkpoint but designed nowhere: the fourth wow verdict lands on a demo whose pages are 'symmetric with W1.2' in the same export grammar, same Oak identity — the owner's fourth look at the same visual language — and the only counterweight is a 'differentiation line' in the checkpoint notes, not an authored design decision.
frameFindings.evidence: W5.2: 'The demo's OWN page set named in the export's grammar, symmetric with W1.2… the checkpoint carries a differentiation line (what makes this demo visually its own thing)' — a reporting obligation with no story producing the thing it reports. Identity switching is out of scope for this demo (§Out of scope), so it cannot differentiate by identity either.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: W5.2's page-set rows name the differentiating design decision at authoring time (distinct page subjects, compositions, or a capability styled-components uniquely showcases), recorded in the page-set artefact where the W0.7 instrument and the checkpoint can judge it.

frameFindings.claim: The showcase page the owner rejected 'out of hand as incompetent' keeps rendering until its per-page W4 migration lands — through the whole of W2 and W3 — despite the owner's requirement being its removal.
frameFindings.evidence: W4.2: 'No standalone delete story. Per page, in one landing: … the old markup removed' — removal is coupled to migration, and W4 sits after W2 ∥ W3 in the sequencing chain. Nothing in W1 retires or replaces the rejected surface when the W1.5 probe pages land in the same workspace.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: When W1.5's probe pages land in the existing showcase workspace, the rejected page's route is replaced or redirected in the same landing (a dated interim act, not a stopgap: the landed state at every moment shows only surfaces the owner has not rejected).
